title: In-running exit price of fallers as a censored performance observation
one_line: Treat a horse that fell or pulled up as a censored run and impute how well it was going from the lowest in-play price it reached before exit, instead of reading the run as blank or last.
definition: Inputs: race_results comment; betfair_prices bsp, ipmin, ip_vol (win). For each earlier jumps run ending fell/unseated/brought down/pulled up (regexes at model/blocks/jumps_form.py:52-53): q = 1/ipmin (best in-running chance reached), q0 = 1/bsp, x = logit(q) - logit(q0). Imputation: (1) in rating updates (market rating, form windows) the run counts as a fractional win of weight q_n = q / sum over the field of 1/ipmin, not as missing or last; (2) its figure is set to the finishers' figure at rank round((1 - q_n) x N). Features: x of last exit, mean x of last 3 exits, flag 'fell with ipmin <= 0.5 x bsp', gap between imputed windows and DNF-as-last windows, race z and gap-to-best of each. Falls and pull-ups kept apart (pulled up with x near 0 = beaten; faller with large x = unlucky). Edge cases: exit before any shortening gives x = 0; ip_vol under a floor shrinks x to 0. Earlier days only.
data_needed: Held: race_results (comment, placing), betfair_prices (bsp, ipmin, ip_vol; from 31 Dec 2017 per ledger open-close-inventory-1101).
card_time: Fully computable before 06:00: uses only runs from earlier days (Betfair price files lag one day).
mechanism: About 16% of jumps runs end with no finishing position (the block's own priors 0.06 + 0.10, model/blocks/jumps_form.py:49), so the form book shows F or P and the served features read unknown or last. The in-running market watched the horse travel. The morning price handles 'fell last time' crudely; people who watched the replay correct it by the off.
nearest_known: inrunning block (ir_: in-play low/high vs BSP of past runs, beaten runs traded <= 2.0) and form_variants DNF-as-last; analysts' hand notes 'fell two out when going well'. Step beyond: a censoring-aware imputation for non-completers that feeds rating updates rather than a side feature.
novelty_check: Repo grep for faller/in-play patterns: 0 files; repo_blocks map lists ir_ only for finishers' lows. world_academic nearest is Brown and Yang 2017 (in-running volume predicts outcome). No web search spent on it - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Drop-in block on the cached matrix, jumps rows; baseline = served base plus jumps_form. Pass: paired error on jumps rows improves by more than the placebo block's spread on the same rows (noise bar 0.0007 on 11 folds, ledger iter114), and x of the last exit predicts ln(morningwap/BSP) at the next run with walk-forward t > 3.

check.repo_evidence: model/blocks/inrunning.py:9-18 already builds ir_lowr_l1/m3 = log(in-play low / BSP) for every past run with a price record, fallers included (main -0.0008 L:iter109; blend -0.0002 unresolved L:iter110). form_variants.py:21 reads non-finishers as last. jumps_form adds -0.0006 on jumps, unresolved (L:iter117-nh-vs-flat). Differs: conditions the low on exit type and imputes a finish. market_rating reads BSPs, not results - nothing to impute there.
check.data_evidence: betfair_prices bsp, ipmin, ip_vol (betfair_prices.py:355-365; from 31 Dec 2017, L:open-close-inventory-1101; win IPMIN sound, L:place-fields-check-1002). race_results comment from 2012 (L:career-truncation). ip_vol is the runner's whole in-play volume, not volume at the low.
check.leakage_notes: none found - past runs only. Price files lag a day, so a run yesterday has no record at 06:00: leave NaN in training too.

title: Franking by absence - rivals who never came back
one_line: Score a past race, and the whole meeting, by how many of its runners have failed to reappear on schedule: an excess of absentees marks a race that damaged horses and a form line biased upward.
definition: Fit on earlier data a discrete-time survival model of days-to-next-run after a run: cells of code x age band x month x finishing third, trainer effect shrunk (k = 30 runs). For today's horse i whose last race r was D days ago, for every rival j in r: S_j = modelled probability j has run again within D days; R_j = 1 if it has (to yesterday). Race harm H_r = sum(S_j - R_j) / sqrt(sum S_j(1 - S_j)). Meeting harm H_m: same over all other runners at that course-day. Features: H_r and H_m for the last run, days-decayed mean over the last 3 runs (half-life 120 days), H x firmness of that day's clock going allowance, and rivals' franking rates re-weighted by 1/S_j (selection-corrected form line). Shrinkage: H set to 0 when sum S_j < 3 (too soon to tell). Edge: end-of-season races use the code's seasonal survival curve; retired/sold-abroad horses are indistinguishable from injured ones (accepted noise).
data_needed: Held: race_results only (dates, horse, trainer, track, code, placing).
card_time: Computable before 06:00 from history to yesterday; H for a recent race updates daily as rivals reappear or fail to.
mechanism: Form is franked only by rivals who run again - survivors. A race on jarring ground or at a punishing pace leaves victims who simply vanish from the record, so its form line reads better than it was and today's runner out of it carries hidden damage risk. Yards and vets know; the morning price reads the visible form.
nearest_known: form_lines / future_form blocks (rivals' next-run results) and veterinary survival models of career length (world_adjacent: 'hazard of non-reappearance as form signal not seen'). Step beyond: the censored absences themselves, as a z-score of the race and the meeting.
novelty_check: Repo grep 'reappear': only a comment at model/stage_f.py:131 and a test; no block. world_adjacent map flags the idea as unseen. No web search spent - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Held data only. Block on the cached matrix against the served base (which holds fl_). Pass: 11-fold paired error better than the 0.0007 noise bar (ledger iter114); and H_r predicts the horse's next-run finish against its BSP chance and ln(morningwap/BSP) with walk-forward t > 3, same sign in both halves of the years.

check.repo_evidence: No block or query: 'reappear' only in a comment at model/stage_f.py:131. Nearest: form_lines (fl_, served, -0.0038 L:iter59) and future_form (ff_, -0.0003 L:iter90) read rivals who DID run again; hx_lr_nonfin (last race's non-completers) retired +0.0001 (L:iter109). Open lead 3 'franked form' (reports/model_review_1111.md:85) is rivals' rating change, not absences.
check.data_evidence: race_results race_date, horse, trainer, track, race_type, age, placing_numerical; complete from 2010 (L:career-truncation). Not held: runs abroad, point-to-points, entries/non-runner history (repo_data map section 3), so sold, exported and retired horses read as absent.
check.leakage_notes: none found if the hazard model is fitted only on rows old enough to be fully observed and R_j stops at yesterday. Bias, not leak: model/freshness_features.py:25 says the history has missing months - false absences.

title: Clock-going nowcast and going-surprise exposure per horse
one_line: Forecast the going the clock will show at each off from a per-course soil water bucket, compare it with the going on the 06:00 card, and multiply the surprise by each horse's own going slope.
definition: (a) Clock going G_m: the meeting's going allowance in seconds per furlong (model/blocks/time_figure.py:12-16). (b) Per course c an hourly bucket W(t+1) = W + P - k_c x ET0 - drain_c x max(W - FC_c, 0), a summer floor W_min by month for watering; link G = a_c + b_c x W. Parameters fitted per course on earlier meetings, shrunk to pooled values (courses under 40 meetings take the pool). (c) At 06:00 run the bucket forward with forecast rain to each off: G_hat. G_stated = the course's mean past allowance for the card's going text. Surprise S = G_hat - G_stated. (d) Horse slope b_i: within-horse regression of (run figure - own mean) on G, shrunk to the sire's slope with 8 pseudo-runs. Features: S, b_i x S, its race z and gap-to-best, P(official going moves a step before the off), S x P(withdrawal) for field-shrink. Edge: all-weather excluded (see the thermal idea); abandoned meetings ignored.
data_needed: Held: times, going text, 86 course coordinates (model/blocks/travel.py). Not held: weather at horse courses (repo_data map section 3). Free public: ERA5-Land hourly precipitation and evaporation via the Copernicus Climate Data Store (free account); card-time forecast from a free forecast feed (ECMWF open data or similar - licence for commercial use to be checked, unverified this session).
card_time: 06:00: bucket state from reanalysis/observations to 05:00 plus the forecast to each off time. Can be refreshed later in the morning.
mechanism: The going at the off differs from the 06:00 card's in 27% of cases (ledger card-vs-results-1110). When the clerk updates, going-dependent horses move in price and non-runners follow. The label is coarse and lags the ground; a physical state per course anticipates the update by hours, and the horse's slope says which prices will move.
nearest_known: Open lead 10 'rain since declarations, forecast going against preferred going' (reports/model_review_1111.md:92); soil water-balance thesis (mean-going prediction reported poor) and the weather-to-going regressions on world_adjacent. Step beyond: the target is the clock allowance not the label, drainage is fitted per course, and the output is surprise x per-horse slope on a continuous scale.
novelty_check: Repo grep water balance / soil moisture / evapotranspiration: 0 files. world_adjacent lists the 2006 thesis and an Irish regression predicting the label only. No dedicated web search.
first_test: Fetch reanalysis for the 86 coordinates 2018-2026. Test 1: walk-forward, does G_hat beat 'stated going only' at predicting realised G_m (pass: MAE down by 10% or more). Test 2: does b_i x S predict ln(morningwap/BSP) from betfair_prices (pass: walk-forward t > 3) and improve the closing model on the recorded marks.

check.repo_evidence: No code (grep soil/rain/evapotranspiration/ERA5 in model, research, scripts: 0 files). But the idea is the repository's own open lead 10: 'Weather and going change - rain since declarations, forecast going against preferred going; needs a card-time source' (reports/model_review_1111.md:92; gap noted at :73). Clock allowance exists (model/blocks/time_figure.py:12-16); going-conditional form cf_ -0.0002 (L:iter57).

Forecast-feed licence unverified.
check.leakage_notes: Three problems. (1) Backtesting with reanalysis rain between 06:00 and the off is perfect foresight - use forecasts as issued before 06:00. (2) Reanalysis cannot supply the 05:00 state live - needs an observation feed. (3) race_results going is the final going, not the 06:00 text; the surprise is testable only on archived cards from 14 Jul 2026.

title: Crosswind echelon - wind-vector forecast of the day's draw-side and cover bias
one_line: On straight courses, project the forecast wind onto the straight: the leeward flank of the field is sheltered by the windward flank, and a headwind raises the value of cover for hold-up horses.
definition: Inputs: bearing of each course's straight (OpenStreetMap geometry; straight-course trips from model/abm/track.py:35-36), 10 m wind vector at the off hour at the course coordinates, stall, field size, run-style score (pace engine). Components: h = headwind (m/s, positive into the runners), x = crosswind signed toward the high-stall side. Features: x x (stall_pct - 0.5) (lee-side advantage), |x| x field size, h x hold-up score, h x front-runner score, gust ratio, and for round courses h in the home straight x style. Coefficients are learned per course-trip and shrunk to a pooled coefficient (k = 200 races). Edge cases: fields under 8 get zero crosswind term (no flank to shelter behind); stalls positioned centre vs rail handled through the draw engine's renumbered stall; wind under 3 m/s set to zero.
data_needed: Held: stall, field, run style, results. Not held: wind history (ERA5 hourly 10 m wind, Copernicus Climate Data Store, free account) and straight bearings (OpenStreetMap, measured once per course).
card_time: 06:00 with the forecast wind for each off time; refreshable later in the morning.
mechanism: Drafting is measured in racing (Spence et al. 2012, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3391435). In a crosswind cover exists on one flank only, as in a cycling echelon; in a headwind leaders pay more. The served draw bias is a course average; wind makes the bias of the day. The market learns it after the first straight races; the forecast exists at 06:00.
nearest_known: Ragozin / Thoro-Graph wind corrections to past figures (world_practice 1); a clerk blaming freak wind for a far-side bias at York (https://racingpost.com/news/britain/freak-wind-blamed-for-ebor-festival-track-bias-and-drop-in-attendances-auyZF7s1VhHO). Step beyond: a signed crosswind x stall and headwind x style forecast of today's bias.
novelty_check: One web search (crosswind, draw bias, straight course): only the York anecdote and generic draw-bias articles; no study isolating wind direction as a draw-bias predictor. Repo grep crosswind/headwind: only sources/noaa_isd.py (greyhound weather).
first_test: Wind for straight-course races 2012-2026. Regress race-centred pounds on x x (stall_pct - 0.5) with course-trip draw effects. Pass: pooled t > 3 and the same sign at 70% or more of courses with 200+ races; then whether the term predicts ln(morningwap/BSP) for races after the first on the card.

check.repo_evidence: No wind in the horse path (grep crosswind/headwind: only sources/noaa_isd.py, greyhound tracks). Relatives all failed: shape/draw rebuild -0.0002 and -0.0000 (L:iter18, L:iter25), draw_v2 -0.0004/-0.0009 (L:iter35, L:iter54), pace_v2 +0.0009 (L:iter35); draw 'small on average and priced', projected leaders A/E 0.91-1.08 (L:pace-draw-bias). Geometry holds straight lengths only, no bearings (model/abm/track.py:37-40).
check.data_evidence: Held: stall, runners, stall_positioning, run style. Wind: hourly direction and speed from NOAA ISD already coded for greyhound tracks (sources/noaa_isd.py:14-16), horse courses not fetched. Straight bearings not held - one-off measurement. As-issued wind forecasts: no source held.
check.leakage_notes: Observed wind at the off hour is not known at 06:00: use it only for the hindsight step; the served feature needs the forecast as issued before 06:00. Whether the card carries stall_positioning at 06:00 is unverified.

title: Stamina limit as an interval-censored dose-response
one_line: Model each horse's stamina as a hidden threshold in effort units and treat every past run as a pass/fail assay that bounds it from one side, with a pedigree prior.
definition: Latent limit L_i in effort-furlongs (see the effort-furlongs idea; first version: furlongs x a going factor). Each earlier run is an assay at dose E_r x p_r (p_r = pace multiplier from race time vs standard). y = 1 'failed to stay' if the comment has weakened|tired|faded|no extra|stopped|tailed off in its final clause, or pulled up after weakening, or in-play low <= 0.5 x BSP and beaten over 10 lengths; y = 0 'stayed' if stayed on|kept on|ran on|won. Other runs carry no information and are dropped. Likelihood P(y = 1) = Phi((dose - L_i)/sigma); L_i ~ Normal(sire mean + damsire mean + age term, tau^2); fitted by EM, refit yearly walk-forward. Features: P(stays today) = 1 - Phi((E_today - L_hat)/sqrt(sigma^2 + var L_hat)), posterior sd, E_today - L_hat, race z. Horses with no informative runs take the pedigree prior; a win at a dose is weighted double.
data_needed: Held: comments (from 2012), trips, going, times, betfair_prices ipmin/bsp, sire and damsire.
card_time: Before 06:00: limits from history; today's dose from card trip and going (the going nowcast can replace the stated going).
mechanism: Staying is a cliff, not a slope: below the limit trip hardly matters, above it the horse stops. Averaged figures blur the cliff, and positions cannot tell 'did not stay' from 'not good enough' - comments and in-running lows can. The market prices a step up in trip from pedigree and guesswork, so the morning price is weakest exactly there.
nearest_known: jf_complete_3m and jf_stay_gap (model/blocks/jumps_form.py:27-30), distance preference (best-NFP trip), Benter's distance-preference slope (world_practice 13); probit bioassay from toxicology. Step beyond: a per-horse threshold bounded by censored pass/fail runs, in energy units, with a hierarchical prior.
novelty_check: Maps read: no threshold or censored stamina model in repo_features, repo_blocks or the two world maps; repo grep for critical speed / speed-duration: 0 files. No web search spent - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Held data, dose = furlongs x going factor. On rows where today's dose exceeds the horse's previous maximum: does P(stays) predict finish against the BSP chance and ln(morningwap/BSP) (walk-forward t > 3); block gain on those rows above the placebo block's spread.

'weakened' (model/comment_features.py:43) +0.0019 (L:iter45); form at today's trip cf_ -0.0002 (L:iter57); sire aptitude -0.0006 (L:iter52), pedigree four readings rejected; jf_stay_gap/jf_complete_3m in jumps_form -0.0006 on jumps, unresolved (L:iter117-nh-vs-flat). check.leakage_notes: none found - comment and ipmin are read from earlier runs only and the fit is yearly walk-forward. Today's dose uses the 06:00 going, which differs from the result's on 27% of card rows (L:card-vs-results-1110).

title: Fitness-fatigue impulse response with race-hardness impulses
one_line: Turn a horse's run history into two decaying states - slow fitness and fast fatigue - where each race is an impulse sized by how hard it was, with yard-specific gains.
definition: Impulse of earlier run s: w_s = 1 + a1 x z(race time vs standard net of going allowance) + a2 x 1(beaten under 2 lengths or won by under 1 and comment has ridden|driven|all out) + a3 x (effort-furlongs - 8)/8 + a4 x softness of clock going; non-completers 0.5. Fitness F(t) = sum w_s exp(-(t - t_s)/tau1); fatigue A(t) = sum w_s exp(-(t - t_s)/tau2), tau1 > tau2 (start 45 and 8 days; grid-fitted walk-forward by code and age band). Trainer gains k1, k2 shrunk to pooled values (50 pseudo-runners). Features: F, A, F - rho x A, race z and gap-to-best, F relative to the horse's own past peak F (first-run-back deficit), predicted days to its optimum, and last impulse w. Edge: debutants NaN; runs before a 300-day break down-weighted by the decay itself.
data_needed: Held: race dates, times, margins, comments, going, trainer.
card_time: Before 06:00: date arithmetic on history plus today's date.
mechanism: Races are the only training load on public record. If fitness fades slowly and fatigue fast, the best interval depends on how hard the last race was and on the yard. The repository's quick-returner rule (1-4 days) beats the morning price (reports/strategy_research_2026-11-04.md:28-48): the early market over-prices fatigue in one cell. A fitted response curve generalises that cell to every gap and every race hardness.
nearest_known: freshness block (fr_: gap vs usual, workload 30/60/90 days, runs since break) and US sheet players' 'bounce'. The Banister impulse-response model is standard for human athletes. Step beyond: two time constants, graded impulses and trainer-specific gains on race results.
novelty_check: One web search (fitness-fatigue impulse-response model, racehorse race results): human-athlete uses only, no racehorse application found. Repo grep banister / fitness-fatigue: 0 files.
first_test: Held data. Block against the served base (which holds fr_): pass on the 0.0007 noise bar over 11 folds (ledger iter114). Second read: does F - rho x A raise the steamer model's top-5% A/E (1.155, reports/strategy_research_2026-11-04.md:124-143) when added to its inputs.

Differs: two exponential kernels, graded impulses, yard gains.

title: Oestrous phase clock recovered from a filly's own run residuals
one_line: For fillies and mares in the breeding season, anchor a 21-day cycle on their own unexplained poor run and use today's phase on that lattice as a feature, with males and winter as placebos.
definition: Population: females, April-September. Residual of earlier run k: e_k = finishing performance less market expectation (won - BSP probability and NFP - BSP-rank-implied NFP; both in the repo). Anchor a = date of the most negative e_k below -1 sd within the last 70 days. Period T = 21 days, tested on a grid 20-23 (average cycle about 21 days: https://www.beva.org.uk/News-Archive/entryid/1103). Phase phi = 2 pi x ((today - a) mod T)/T. Features: cos phi and sin phi damped by exp(-(today - a)/45); in-window flag when (today - a) mod T is within 3 days of 0; for fillies with 4+ runs this season, Lomb-Scargle power of e at 19-24 days against 10-18 and 25-40 days. The same quantities are computed for colts/geldings and for October-February as placebo columns, and the usable signal is female-in-season minus placebo (this removes the three-week fixture lattice). No anchor = NaN.
data_needed: Held: race_results (sex, dates, placing, bfsp).
card_time: Before 06:00: date arithmetic on the filly's own history.
mechanism: A mare in oestrus can run flat; the yard sees it and often runs her anyway. If poor runs recur on a three-week lattice, today's phase is performance information that nobody outside the yard holds at 06:00. Stable money and paddock watchers (visible signs) move the price late, so it may show first in the close.
nearest_known: Folk rule 'fillies are unreliable in spring'; the retired seasonal block (sn_, ledger iter98) uses calendar months. Step beyond: an individual phase recovered from the filly's own residual series, not a calendar average.
novelty_check: One web search (oestrous cycle, race performance, 21-day periodicity): veterinary pieces say poor performance is often attributed to oestrus but no study linking cycle phase to race results was found. Repo grep oestr/estrous: 0 relevant files.
first_test: Held data 2012-2026, runs with gaps <= 45 days after an anchor. Regress next-run residual on the in-window flag with a female x season interaction. Pass: interaction negative with t > 3, placebo groups |t| < 2, same sign in 8 of 11 folds; then the same on ln(morningwap/BSP). Any effect size is unknown; a null is the likeliest single outcome (guess).

check.repo_evidence: grep oestr/estrus/Lomb/periodogram in model, research, scripts, reports: 0 relevant hits. Nearest: L:context-survey (A/E by month 1.0006-1.0033; a horse's own seasonality +0.021; block not built) and seasonal sn_ L:iter98 0.0000. Neither splits by sex or uses an individual phase.

check.leakage_notes: No leak: own earlier runs and today's date. Timing trap, not a leak: the T grid (20-23), the 70-day anchor window, the -1 sd cut and the 3-day window are four tuned knobs - fix one setting before the run or every setting counts as a trial.

title: Survive-then-contest likelihood for jump races
one_line: Model a jump race as a per-obstacle hazard of exit with a shared race frailty, then a Plackett-Luce contest among the survivors, and integrate over survivor sets for each win chance.
definition: Stage 1: per-obstacle exit hazard, logit h = eta_i (horse frailty; prior from sire and trainer; learning term -lambda x log(1 + earlier runs over this obstacle type)) + phi(course, obstacle type) + going + field size + u_r, with u_r ~ Normal(0, omega^2) a race-level frailty (pace, bringing down). A second hazard for pulling up rises with effort beyond the horse's stamina limit. Completion c_i = product of (1 - h). Stage 2: given completer set S, order is Plackett-Luce on strengths from the served forecast. Joint likelihood on results (exits observed from comments, finishers as an order). Win chance p_i = E_u[sum over S of P(S|u) x PL_i(S)], exact for N <= 10, else 2,000 draws. Features: p_i, c_i, p_i minus the contest-only share, expected finishers, P(first two in the forecast both exit). Obstacle counts from public course guides; without them use trip-based counts by code.
data_needed: Held: results, comments (exit type), going, field, trainer, sire. Free public: obstacles per circuit from course guides (hand-built table).
card_time: Before 06:00: hazards from history, strengths from the 06:00 forecast.
mechanism: In staying and novice chases who gets round decides as much as who is best. One softmax spreads that risk evenly; the true book is a mixture over survivor sets, which shifts probability toward sound jumpers in attritional races and toward the class horse where jumping is easy. The exchange arrives at that mixture by the off; a 06:00 softmax cannot.
nearest_known: jumps_form fall and pulled-up rates as plain features (model/blocks/jumps_form.py:16-30); exploded logit with eased runners censored, named future work (repo_models 11); competing-risks and cure models in survival analysis. Step beyond: an explicit two-stage generative likelihood with a shared race frailty.
novelty_check: Maps read: no hazard-plus-contest model in repo_models or world_academic (ordering models there are Harville, Henery, Stern, discount). No web search spent - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Held data 2012-2026. Fit stage 1; check out-of-sample calibration of c_i by decile and a likelihood-ratio test of omega^2 > 0. Then add p_i features on chase rows: pass if paired error and the race cross-entropy to the BSP book beat the served base plus jumps_form by more than the placebo spread on those rows.

Exits must be read for the horse itself (place code first), not any 'fell' in the comment - the fault recorded in L:iter117.

title: Hoof-traffic wear state of each strip of track
one_line: Carry a decaying physical state per course strip - hooves galloped times wetness, healed by grass growth, reset by rail moves - to predict today's draw and pace bias before a race is run.
definition: For course c, strip k (Flat round, Flat straight, hurdle, chase) on day t: T = sum over earlier fixtures f within 60 days of runners_f x furlongs_f x wet_f x exp(-(t - t_f)/tau) x (1 - fresh), where wet_f = softness of that day's clock going allowance (or the water-bucket state), tau = 21 days April-September and 60 days otherwise (grid-fitted; with weather data, tau tied to soil temperature above 6C), fresh = 1 when today's rail_move puts racing on ground unused since f. Within-card wear: runners x furlongs of today's earlier races on the strip, known from the card. Features: T, T x (stall_pct - 0.5), T x front-runner score, T x hold-up score, days since the rail last moved, day index within a multi-day meeting, within-card wear x wetness. Coefficients shrunk across courses (k = 300 races). Edge: all-weather uses hours since last meeting only.
data_needed: Held: race_results (fixtures, runners, trips, rail_move, going, times, stall), run-style scores.
card_time: Before 06:00: all inputs are earlier fixtures and today's card (later non-runners change within-card wear slightly).
mechanism: Track bias is made by traffic: the inside strip is cut up in proportion to hooves times wetness and heals with growth. The served draw biases are long-run averages, and in-day bias features failed out of sample (holdout -18.7%, ledger confirm-holdout) because they need the day's own races. Wear state is the part of the day's bias that is predictable at 06:00, before the market sees two races.
nearest_known: Draw engine (rail move, course x trip x going bias with 730-day decay, model/draw_metrics.py), rejected in-day features, practitioners' 'fresh ground' notes. Step beyond: a quantified, decaying wear state built from fixtures already held.
novelty_check: Maps read: repo_features draw engine has no traffic term; world_practice lists daily track-bias notes as unverified hand products. No web search spent - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Held data. Target = the race's draw slope and pace slope of beat-the-market residuals (as model/inday_features.py builds them). Pass: T x stall and T x style terms at t > 3, same sign in both halves of the years; then the block on 11 folds against the 0.0007 noise bar.

In-day bias model/inday_features.py rejected, holdout -18.7% (L:confirm-holdout). Draw/pace rebuilds -0.0002/-0.0000 (L:iter18, iter25), draw_v2 -0.0004/-0.0009 (L:iter35, iter54). Open lead: soft-ground low draws A/E 1.095 z 3.0 (L:pace-draw-bias). Differs: cumulative runners x furlongs x wetness with decay.

title: Effort-furlongs - an energy-equivalent trip for every course, going and code
one_line: Replace the nominal trip with the distance on flat good ground that costs the same energy, built from climb, descent, turning, going and obstacles, and read all stamina evidence in that unit.
definition: For each (course, trip, code): E = d x [1 + alpha x ascent/d_m - beta x descent/d_m + gamma x turn] x g(G) + delta x n_obstacles, in furlong-equivalents. ascent and descent in metres from a 30 m elevation model sampled along the course centreline (OpenStreetMap) from start to finish; turn = sum of |heading change|/radius; G = clock going allowance (or the going text's usual allowance at card time); n_obstacles from course guides. alpha, beta, gamma, delta and g() are fitted once so that E reproduces the course standard times (seconds per furlong by course-trip-code, model/blocks/time_figure.py:10-11) - a regression across about 1,000 course-trip cells, refit yearly. Runner level: E_w = E x (1 + kappa x (weight - 130)/1100). Features: today's E; E minus the horse's mean E in its 3 best-figure runs; E minus the largest E at which it ran within 5 lb of its best; race z. Courses without geometry fall back to nominal trip with a flag.
data_needed: Held: standard times, trips, going, weights; coarse geometry for Flat only (model/abm/track.py:35-36, no elevation). Free public: OpenStreetMap course lines, a 30 m global elevation model (Copernicus DEM), course guides for obstacles - a one-off build, about 86 courses.
card_time: Before 06:00: static course table plus the card's going and weight.
mechanism: Stamina is spent in energy, not furlongs. Two miles uphill on heavy ground over stiff fences draws what two and a half draws on a flat sound track. The card and form book compare trips in furlongs; a common energy unit lets stamina evidence transfer across courses, goings and codes, and flags the 'new trip' that in energy terms is old - or the 'usual trip' that is not.
nearest_known: Trail running's kilometre-effort (distance plus climb); analysts' adjectives 'stiff', 'sharp', 'galloping'; repo distance preference in furlongs and jf_trip_vs_usual (model/blocks/jumps_form.py:31). Step beyond: a fitted energy-equivalent trip per course, trip and going, used as the axis for stamina features.
novelty_check: Repo grep for elevation/ascent: no course elevation anywhere; track geometry table has straight length and bend radius only. world maps: no energy-equivalent distance in racing. No web search spent - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Build E for the courses. Test A: leave-courses-out, do the terms explain standard seconds per furlong beyond trip and code. Test B: swap furlongs for E in the trip features (trip vs usual, distance from best trip); pass on 11 folds against the 0.0007 bar, and on rows where E and nominal trip disagree most (top quintile).

title: Low-sun obstacle forecast from solar geometry and course bearings
one_line: Compute from the sun's elevation and azimuth at each off time, the bearing of each jumping straight and forecast cloud, the chance that fences are omitted or jumped into glare, and price that per horse.
definition: Inputs: off time, date, course coordinates, direction of travel psi of each obstacle-bearing straight (OpenStreetMap, measured once), solar elevation e and azimuth a at the off (standard solar position algorithm, no data needed), forecast cloud cover cl. Glare index per straight g = 1(2 deg < e < 12 deg) x max(0, cos(a - psi)) x (1 - cl). Features: g home straight, g back straight; expected share of the race's obstacles omitted = share sited in straights with g above a threshold g0 (g0 fitted on recorded omissions if result notes are obtained, otherwise on the time signature below); g x horse fall rate (jf_fall_rate); g x latent jumping skill; g x front-runner score (leaders meet the glare unsighted); g x trip. Edge: e under 2 deg or after sunset gives 0; hurdles and fences separate; meetings where races are re-ordered are handled by using the card's off times.
data_needed: Held: off times, course coordinates, fall/pull-up flags, times. Free: solar ephemeris (computed); straight bearings (OpenStreetMap); cloud history from ERA5 (free account). Omission history: no data found in the repo - result notes would need a source.
card_time: 06:00: geometry is exact days ahead; cloud from the morning forecast.
mechanism: In winter obstacles facing a low sun are omitted, often decided close to the race, and a chase with its straight fences out is a different contest: 'a much-reduced jumping test' that hurts good jumpers (https://www.sportinglife.com/racing/news/unsuitable-ground-low-sun-and-autumn-winners-assessed-jumps-analysis-from-phil-turner/235227). The morning price is formed on the advertised race; the sun's position at the off is known in advance to anyone who computes it.
nearest_known: Trade-press commentary on low-sun omissions; no model. Step beyond: forecast the omission and glare from ephemeris and bearings, and express it as a per-horse interaction with jumping.
novelty_check: One web search (low sun, fences omitted, analysis, predict): commentary and forum threads only; no dataset of omissions and no model predicting them from sun angle and course orientation.
first_test: Compute g for all hurdles and chases 2012-2026. Test 1 (signature): are winning times faster against standard and fall rates different in high-g races, against a placebo g with the clock shifted 3 hours. Test 2: does g x fall rate predict finish vs BSP chance and ln(morningwap/BSP), t > 3 with the placebo null.

Nearest input: jf_fall_rate in jumps_form, which did not pass (L:iter117-nh-vs-flat, jumps -0.0006, -0.0016 to +0.0003).

check.leakage_notes: ERA5 is a reanalysis of the weather that happened, not the 06:00 forecast: using it in a backtest leaks. Use clear-sky geometry only, or an archived forecast issued before 06:00. Results carry the actual off time; use the card's time, since races are re-ordered and delayed for low sun.

title: Critical speed and distance reserve fitted per horse from standardised race times
one_line: Fit each horse's two-parameter speed-duration law - a sustainable speed and a finite distance reserve - from its own times at different trips, shrunk to its sire, and extrapolate to today's trip.
definition: Per earlier run: standardised time t* = the seconds the horse would take over the trip at a standard course on good ground = d x standard s/f x (1 + deviation), deviation from the race time net of the meeting going allowance plus beaten lengths in seconds (2.4 m a length, model/blocks/time_figure.py:41), less a weight correction. Fit t* = (d - D_i)/CS_i over the horse's runs at 2+ distinct trips (1.5f apart or more), each run weighted by pace truth (race within 1.5% of standard), with a bivariate normal prior on (CS, D) by sire x sex x age band worth 4 runs. Features: CS_i, D_i (metres), predicted t* at today's trip minus the field's best (converted to lengths), its race z, the trip d0 where the horse's predicted margin over the field median peaks, |d_today - d0|, posterior sd. Where Flat sectionals are held, finishing-speed % tightens D. One-trip horses take the prior with their level shifted.
data_needed: Held: comptime, margins, trips, going, weights; time_figure standards and allowances; sectionals (Flat, partial).
card_time: Before 06:00: history only, plus today's trip.
mechanism: The hyperbolic speed-duration law is established for horses on the treadmill but has not been fitted from races (world_adjacent: 'none found fitted per horse from race or sectional data'). Two numbers per horse turn scattered runs at different trips into a curve that extrapolates to an untried trip, where the market leans on pedigree and running style.
nearest_known: time_figure block (a figure per run, no cross-trip structure), distance preference (best-NFP trip), the race ABM's assumed critical-power parameters (model/abm/agents.py:60 per world_adjacent), Benter's distance-preference slope. Step beyond: the physical two-parameter law fitted per horse from sparse results with hierarchical shrinkage.
novelty_check: Repo grep critical speed / speed-duration: 0 files. world_academic: 'Equine critical-speed primary study tied to race results: none'. No further web search.

Per-run clock figure tf_ (L:iter37 -0.0005). Trip-conditioned figures -0.0002 (L:iter57); sire distance aptitude -0.0006 (L:iter52); pedigree four ways rejected (L:iter49, iter73, iter84). title: Latent jumping skill against course stiffness, with lateral jump bias
one_line: Separate each horse's jumping skill from its galloping ability and each course's obstacle stiffness from who runs there, by a crossed factor model on falls, jumping-error comments and figure deficits.
definition: Jumps runs, three outcomes: (i) fall/unseat (logit); (ii) jumping error in the comment - mistake|blundered|hit|not fluent|jumped slowly|jumped left|jumped right (logit); (iii) figure deficit against the horse's own baseline from bumpers/Flat and clean rounds. Each loads on skill J_i (by obstacle type) and course-obstacle stiffness s_c: logit P = a + s_c - J_i + going + pace + runs-over-obstacle term. Fit by alternating ridge / EM; J_i ~ Normal(sire-line mean, tau^2); s_c shrunk toward public course facts (fence type, padded or birch hurdles, open ditches, downhill fences). Lateral bias B_i = (jumped-left count - jumped-right count)/(n + 4). Features: J_i, its sd, J_i x s_today, race z, slope of J over the last 4 runs (novice learning), B_i x handedness of today's course (track_direction), predicted fence skill for a chase debutant from hurdle skill and sire. Horses with under 2 jumps runs take the prior.
data_needed: Held: comments, results, track_direction, sire, times. Free public: course obstacle facts (hand-built table from course guides and regulator notices).
card_time: Before 06:00: history only.
mechanism: Galloping and jumping are different skills and courses tax them differently. One rating blends both, so a slick jumper is under-rated at a stiff track and over-rated at an easy one, and a horse that jumps left gives ground away going right-handed. Course stiffness net of the horses that run there is published nowhere.
nearest_known: Tracking-based 'Lengths Gained Jumping' and 'Jump Index' (https://www.racingtv.com/raceiq/glossary), analysts' jumping comments, jumps_form fall rates. Step beyond: skill and stiffness identified jointly from results and comments without tracking, plus lateral bias x handedness.
novelty_check: Repo grep: jumping-error phrases are parsed only to keep them out of position reads (model/race_shape.py:82); the retired comments block had no jumping classes (repo_blocks). No web search spent - unverified beyond the maps.
first_test: Fit to 2012-2022; in 2023-2026, on rows where today's s differs most from the horse's past mean s (top quintile): do J x s and B x handedness predict falls/errors and finish vs BSP chance (t > 3); block gain on jumps rows above the placebo spread.

Mistake comments are written mostly for prominent horses, so the error emission correlates with finishing position and price - condition on position. Comment regex must bind to the horse (jf's recorded fault: 'refused to settle', another horse's fall).

title: Dead-weight coupling from each jockey's inferred riding floor
one_line: Infer each jockey's minimum riding weight from the lightest weights he has ridden, and measure today's lead in the cloth: rigid dead weight should cost a horse more than the same pounds of crouching jockey.
definition: Jockey floor m_j(t): the second-lowest actual weight carried by jockey j in the trailing 365 days (as of yesterday; second-lowest guards against typos), requiring 30+ rides, else the pooled floor for his claim band. Dead weight DW = max(0, weight to carry today - m_j) in lb; overweight risk OW = max(0, m_j - weight to carry). Features: DW, DW/weight, race z of DW, OW, change in DW since the horse's last run (same weight, lighter rider = more lead), DW x trip, DW x jumps code, DW x effort-furlongs. Controls built alongside so the model can separate rider quality: claim, jockey's bookings rating (bk_). Edge: weight-for-age and conditions races included; amateur and lady-rider races flagged; card weight is before the claim, so the claim is deducted first.
data_needed: Held: race_results pounds, claim, jockey, dates; card weight and jockey.
card_time: Before 06:00 once the jockey is declared on the card; OW also forecasts overweight announced at the course later in the day.
mechanism: A crouching jockey decouples his mass from the horse's vertical motion (Pfau et al. 2009, Science - cited from the map, unverified this session); lead in the cloth is rigidly coupled and must be accelerated every stride. Two horses 'carrying 9-7' therefore carry different mechanical loads. The belief exists in racing 'without hard evidence' (https://canadianthoroughbred.com/magazine/handicapping/the-weighty-matter-of-weight-assignments-in-racing/), and minimum weights are not in the form data.
nearest_known: Weight features (vs race mean, change), bookings block; folk argument about dead weight. Step beyond: a riding floor inferred from ride history, turning the argument into a measurable per-runner load.
novelty_check: One web search (dead weight, lead cloth, live weight, performance analysis): the belief is discussed, no study comparing dead and live weight found. Repo: minimum riding weight noted as absent from the export (reports/hrb_system_builder_review.md:197).
first_test: Held data, handicaps. Regress race-centred pounds and finish vs BSP chance on DW with horse and jockey fixed effects and the claim as control. Pass: DW coefficient negative at t > 3 within jockey, same sign Flat and jumps; then 11-fold block against the 0.0007 bar.

Existing weight features: weight_vs_avg, weight_vs_min, weight_change_lr (model/custom_metrics.py:1445-1455), hca_; ledger card-weight-check-1111 (weight after claim on the card) registered, unread.

Overweight put up is not a column, so the floor is the lowest allotted weight accepted, not a weighed-out weight.
check.leakage_notes: No result leak if the 365-day window ends yesterday. title: Thermal hidden going on all-weather surfaces
one_line: Forecast the clock going and run-style bias of wax-bound all-weather tracks from surface temperature at each off time, because the official going says 'standard' whatever the surface is doing.
definition: For all-weather meetings: surface-temperature proxy theta = 2 m air temperature + c1 x shortwave radiation - c2 x wind speed at the off hour (c1, c2 fitted). Per course and surface family (Polytrack, Tapeta, Fibresand history; resurfacing dates as breakpoints) fit the meeting's clock going allowance G = f_c(theta, rain in the last 6 h, hours since the previous meeting as a harrowing proxy, month), walk-forward. At 06:00, with forecast theta for each off: features G_hat, G_hat minus the usual allowance for the stated going, G_hat x front-runner score, G_hat x hold-up score, G_hat x the horse's slope of figure on all-weather clock going (shrunk, 8 pseudo-runs), change in theta across the card (afternoon to floodlit evening). Edge: courses with a surface change are refit from the change date with the family prior.
data_needed: Held: all-weather times, going text, run-style scores. Not held: weather at courses - ERA5 hourly temperature, radiation, wind (Copernicus Climate Data Store, free account); forecast feed at card time.
card_time: 06:00 with forecast temperature and radiation per off time.
mechanism: Wax-bound surfaces change with temperature: race times tracked temperature at one US synthetic track (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20525055/) and trade reports tie cold, loose Polytrack to kickback and speed bias (https://www.drf.com/news/cooler-weather-affects-polytrack). The official going hides it under 'standard'. Clock going exists only after racing; temperature at the off is forecastable at 06:00.
nearest_known: Peterson et al. 2010 (times vs temperature, one track, no running styles), trade anecdotes; time_figure going allowance (post-race). Step beyond: a card-time forecast of clock going and pace bias per UK/IE all-weather course.
novelty_check: One web search (synthetic surface temperature, wax, race times, front-runner bias): the Del Mar study and a UK laboratory study of wax-bound surfaces; front-runner effect only anecdotal; no predictive use found.
first_test: Weather for the all-weather courses 2012-2026 plus held times. Pass 1: theta explains G out of sample for each surface family (t > 3, walk-forward MAE below 'stated going only'). Pass 2: G_hat x run style predicts finish vs BSP chance and ln(morningwap/BSP).

check.repo_evidence: Same construction exists for greyhounds: wx_pred_variant, 'how much faster the track should run in this weather, learnt per track on earlier years' (reports/greyhound_metrics_registry.md:81-88; sources/noaa_isd.py). title: Coupled hidden yard-health state with a fade-signature emission
one_line: Filter a hidden health state for every yard from its runners' 'travelled then emptied' signature, runner-count anomalies and market residuals, with infection pressure from neighbouring yards.
definition: Daily state z per yard in {well, incubating, sick, recovering}; hidden Markov model, forward-filtered to yesterday. Emissions per runner: (a) won - BSP probability and NFP against price rank; (b) fade signature = in-play low <= 0.6 x BSP yet beaten over 8 lengths, or comment weakened quickly|stopped|eased|pulled up; (c) runner-count anomaly = runners in the trailing 10 days against a Poisson expectation from the same weeks of earlier years; (d) late non-runner share where cards are archived (from 14 Jul 2026). title: Stale reduction-factor basis: the non-runner cut as a forecastable price
one_line: Measure, per runner and snapshot, the gap between Betfair's adjustment factor and the live market probability, weight it by a withdrawal hazard, and add the expected cut gain or loss to every bet's bar.
definition: Inputs: recorded books (adjustment_factor, removal_utc, best prices; betfair_recorder.py:57,169). For runner j at snapshot t: p_j = normalised mid probability, f_j = adjustment_factor/100 (0 if under 0.025 - threshold to verify against Betfair's rules). Basis b_j = f_j - p_j. Withdrawal hazard h_j(t) = logistic on ln(mid_j / price implied by f_j) (drift since the factor was set), minutes to the off, going changed since declaration, yard's past removal rate (shrunk, k=30 declarations), fitted walk-forward on removals since 30 Sep 2026. For a back on i: expected cut drag D_i = sum over j != i of h_j x [(1 - f_j)/(1 - p_j) - 1]. Trade only if expected CLV + D_i clears the bar; a lay on i carries -D_i. Edge cases: factor refresh times (measure them first); two removals compound; place markets use a different rule - exclude.
data_needed: Held: betfair_live_markets / marks with adjustment_factor and removal_utc from 30 Sep 2026; live_orders. Betfair Historic BASIC from Jan 2024 also carries removed runners (sources/open_close.py:150 filters them).
card_time: Later-morning: computed at each decision 05:15-10:00 UK from the book then; the yard habit term is known before 06:00.
mechanism: A horse with a problem drifts before it is withdrawn. If Betfair's factor lags the price, the cut applied to matched backs on the others is larger than the market's true re-formation, so backers pay the difference every time. The record shows cuts take about half the fill edge (before 10:00: +10.7% at the fill, +5.5% after the cuts; ledger live-by-hour-1104). Nobody prices this gap in the morning book.
nearest_known: Ledger reductions-1021 (expected factor by price band) and removal-tilt-replay-1109 (market-level removal forecast from field, minutes, Ireland). The step: a per-runner basis between the factor and the live probability, joined to a per-runner hazard driven by drift.
novelty_check: Ledger grep for 'adjustment factor': 0 hits. One web search: forum and guide pages note a factor can lag a drifted price (theracingforum.co.uk/forums/topic/betfair-and-the-reduction-factors/), no systematic rule or forecast found. Whether the factor is in fact stale is unverified.
first_test: On every recorded removal since 30 Sep 2026 with f >= 2.5%: compare f_j with p_j at the last snapshot before removal_utc. Pass 1: mean ln((1-f)/(1-p)) below zero with a race-clustered 90% interval, and predicted by pre-removal drift. Pass 2: replay as reductions-1021 - bar on CLV + D_i against the price-band bar, CLV x stake after cuts, day bootstrap above zero, deflated Sharpe >= 0.95.

title: Learned forgiveness: the market's verdict on each past run
one_line: Use how far the next closing price moved after each past run, relative to that run's result surprise, as a per-run reliability weight on all form, and forecast it for the latest run.
definition: For run k of a horse with a next run: s_k = race-centred pounds beaten (or NFP) minus its expectation given that day's BSP share (lagged fit). u_k = next market reading minus the rating before run k (y and m of model/blocks/market_rating.py:13). Fit g(s) = E[u | s] by code on earlier days (monotone spline). Forgiveness phi_k = 1 - u_k/g(s_k), clipped to [-1, 2], defined when |g(s_k)| > 0.05, shrunk to 0 with weight |g|/(|g|+0.1). (a) Market-weighted form: recompute form-window measures with run weights clip(1 - phi_k, 0, 2). (b) Latest run has no successor: train a boosted model of phi on the run's circumstances (going against the horse's usual, trip change, draw, comment classes, yard form that month, gap, headgear, class move); feature fg_last = predicted phi x g(s_last), in rating units, plus its race z-score.
data_needed: Held: race_results (bfsp, distances, comments, going) 2010-2026; market rating block.
card_time: All from runs before today; fully known before 06:00 UK.
mechanism: The closing crowd knows excuses that never reach a database - jockey and vet reports, video, yard illness. Its next price shows which runs it believed. Thin 06:00 books are set largely off raw form, so a bad run of a type the close habitually forgives is over-counted in the morning and corrected by the off.

title: Reliability-weighted book reconciliation: fresh runners price the stale ones
one_line: Replace proportional normalisation of the thin morning book with a sum-to-one estimate that moves each runner's price in proportion to how wide, shallow and stale its own quote is.
definition: Inputs per runner i at snapshot t: best back B_i, best lay L_i, sizes at 3 levels, age a_i = polls since B_i, L_i or last traded changed. Mid probability m_i = (1/B_i + 1/L_i)/2. Quote variance v_i = ((1/B_i - 1/L_i)/2)^2 x (1 + a_i/a0) / (1 + depth_i/d0), a0 = 3 polls, d0 = GBP50 (to tune on pre-registered folds). Reconciled x_i = m_i + (1 - sum m) x v_i / sum v, floored at 0.001, renormalised. Features: ln(x_i / proportional m_i); v_i share; and x_i as the 'market now' input of the closing model. Also compute the cross-implied back price 1/(1 - sum over j != i of 1/L_j) where the sum is below 1 and flag when it beats B_i (the native quote is dominated). Runners with no lay quote: L = 1000.
data_needed: Held: betfair_live_markets books (3 levels, sizes, last traded) from 30 Sep 2026; full ladder stream from 12 Nov 2026.
card_time: Later-morning: computed from the book at each decision 05:15-10:00 UK.
mechanism: At 08:00 the median market has GBP1,423 matched (ledger open-close-inventory-1101): many runners show one stale order. The book must still sum to one, so the well-quoted runners jointly fix the price of the badly quoted ones. Proportional normalisation spreads the error over everyone; later money corrects exactly the runners this estimate moves.

title: Ghost runs: prices of withdrawn horses as hidden rating readings
one_line: Every time a horse was declared, traded and then withdrawn, the market measured it; feed those prices into the market rating and read the pre-withdrawal drift as a tell.
definition: Source rows: runners with status REMOVED and a price before removal (Betfair Historic BASIC from Jan 2024; live record from 30 Sep 2026). Ghost reading y_g = ln(p_j) + C_j exactly as market_rating.py:13, p_j = j's share of the book at the last snapshot before removal (all then-active runners). Reading variance R_g = lambda x R, lambda >= 1 chosen by one-step predictive likelihood on days before a fixed date; larger when the removal is more than 3 hours before the off. Ghost readings enter the Kalman filter in date order with real ones. Extra features: gh_n (ghost readings in 365 days), gh_days (days since the last), gh_drift = ln(price at removal / first price that day), gh_since_run (1 if a ghost reading postdates the last real run). Horses matched by name and selection id; skip removals with no trade.
data_needed: Held: Betfair Historic BASIC (all countries, Jan 2024 on); betfair_live_markets from 30 Sep 2026. race_results has no non-runners (repo_data map).
card_time: All from earlier days; known before 06:00 UK.
mechanism: A results database has no row for a horse that did not run, so models and form-driven morning quotes never see that the horse was 5/2 when taken out last week. title: Market-implied going shift read from the meeting's cross-section of moves
one_line: Infer the market's revised view of the going at a meeting from how prices of ground-sensitive horses moved in its other races, then apply that shift to runners whose books have not moved yet.
definition: Loading beta_i: slope of the horse's past market readings (market_rating.py:13) on the going scale, shrunk to its sire's mean then to zero (k = 10 readings). title: Substitution-aware re-formation: cross-elasticities of the book beyond renormalisation
one_line: Model how a move or withdrawal of one runner redistributes probability to its close substitutes rather than pro rata, and forecast the knock-on moves the morning book has not made.
definition: Similarity K_ij in [0,1] between runners of a race: mean of indicators/kernels - same trainer, same owner, same projected run style (pace engine), same sign of going loading, adjacent price rank, draw within 2 stalls. Model: d ln p_i = -dp_j/(1 - p_j) x [1 + theta x (K_ij - Kbar_j)] + error, Kbar_j the share-weighted mean similarity to j; theta fitted by weighted least squares, separately for moves and removals, ridge-shrunk. Features at decision time: ko_i = sum over j of theta x (K_ij - Kbar_j) x (forecast share change of j from the closing model) / (1 - p_j); nr_i = same with p_j x removal hazard for j. Two-runner races: zero.

title: Horse-specific performance variance from place-versus-win price history
one_line: Identify each horse's consistency from how the market has priced it to place relative to win, carry it as a trait, and price today's race with a field of unequal variances.

title: Window-by-window population signatures scaled by expected crowd size
one_line: Fit a separate move model for each pre-race window, treat each as the taste of the bettors who arrive then, and add them up scaled by how big each crowd will be for this race.
definition: Windows from Betfair Historic BASIC: W1 T-24h to T-60, W2 T-60 to T-15, W3 T-15 to T-1, W4 T-1 to BSP; from the recorded marks also W0 06:00-10:00. For each window s fit m_s(x): boosted regression of the change in ln book share on card features, walk-forward. Crowd scale c_s(race) = expected share of the race's pre-off turnover traded in window s, from an empirical-Bayes table by course x class band x weekday x televised/festival flag (pp_vol and morning_vol in betfair_prices; live marks for the split). Forecast move = sum over s of (c_s / mean c_s) x m_s(x). Features: each m_s(x), the scaled sum, and the disagreement m_W3 - m_W1.
data_needed: Held: Betfair Historic BASIC from Jan 2024; betfair_prices volumes from 2018; marks from 30 Sep 2026. Televised flag: free public TV schedules - no history held.
card_time: Models and crowd table from earlier days; all features at 06:00.
mechanism: Stable money, bookmaker hedges and the television and on-course public arrive at different times with different tastes. One pooled move model averages opposing signatures; the edge by hour in the live record (ledger live-by-hour-1104) says the windows differ. A Saturday handicap and a Monday seller differ in which crowd dominates.
nearest_known: The served steamer model (one regression of log(morning/BSP); reports/strategy_research_2026-11-04.md:124-143); Johnson, Jones and Tang 2006 odds-path shapes. The step: window-specific attribute signatures combined by an ex-ante crowd-size forecast.

title: Owner crowd size: racing-club members as late money
one_line: Classify each owner as club, syndicate, partnership or individual and estimate the head-count behind the horse, as a measure of small late bets that arrive regardless of its chance.
definition: Parse the owner string: club = contains 'Racing Club', 'Club', 'Owners Group' or similar; syndicate = 'Syndicate', 'Partnership', roman-numeral suffix, or three or more '&'/comma names; else individual or company. Crowd proxy n_o = for club/syndicate types, distinct horses run under that owner name in the last 365 days (a larger operation has more members), log-scaled. Features: oc_type, oc_size, and per-owner shrunk mean (k = 20 runs) of ln(BSP share / T-60 share) and of ln(T-60 share / morning share) - the late and the early move kept apart; oc_type x Saturday. mechanism: A club with thousands of members produces thousands of small bets on its runner, mostly on the day and late. A sole gambling owner produces early, informed money. title: Card-order attention with the alphabetical natural experiment
one_line: Where saddlecloth numbers are assigned alphabetically among equal weights, card position is unrelated to ability, so its effect on public money and the late move is a clean attention measure.
definition: Step 1 (verify in data): in non-handicaps, share of races where card_no order equals (weight descending, horse name ascending). Use only race groups passing. Within each equal-weight group of size g >= 3: co_i = (rank of card_no in the group - 1)/(g - 1). Features: co_i; top_line = 1 if card_no = 1; for all races, card_no rank residualised on weight rank. Targets to read: the industry-SP minus BSP share wedge, ln(BSP share / morning share), and the winner with the BSP as offset. Dead-heats in names and reserves excluded.
data_needed: Held: race_results card_no, pounds, horse, race_type, odds, bfsp; betfair_prices morningwap.
card_time: From the 06:00 card.
mechanism: People choosing from a list favour its top lines (the ballot-order effect), and exchange and bookmaker screens list by cloth number by default. Late recreational money therefore leans to low numbers. In handicaps number 1 is the top weight, so the effect is confounded; alphabetical numbering removes the confound.
nearest_known: Post-position efficiency studies (Canfield, Fauman and Ziemba 1987); fast-sounding names over-bet (SSRN 3469641). The step: list position as an exogenous attention shock with an alphabetical instrument.
novelty_check: One web search: no study of card order, saddlecloth number or alphabetical primacy in racing odds found. Ledger scan for 'alphabet', 'card_no': 0 hits. The alphabetical numbering rule itself is from memory - to verify in the data.

title: SP auction imbalance decides where the hedge is laid
one_line: Read the starting-price pool's one-sidedness from the recorded near and far prices and SP stakes, forecast the BSP's gap to the last exchange price, and lay on whichever venue is forecast cheaper.
definition: Inputs at the T-3 and T-1 marks: mid, sp_near, sp_far, sp_back_taken, sp_lay_taken (betfair_recorder.py:60,171). z_i = ln(sp_far / mid); w_i = SP pool size / (SP pool size + exchange money within 5 ticks of the mid). Model: ln(BSP / mid at T-1) = a x z x w + b x ln(sp_near / mid), fitted walk-forward by price band. Rule for each open back: if the forecast BSP exceeds the T-1 lay price by more than the spread plus a margin, lay on the exchange now; otherwise leave the SP lay. Subtract this trader's own SP lay liability from the pool before computing z (self-impact).
data_needed: Held: books with SP fields from 30 Sep 2026 (SP_AVAILABLE asked from 8 Oct per CLAUDE.md); live_orders.
card_time: Near the off (T-3 to T-1).
mechanism: The BSP clears SP backers against SP layers and the exchange's unmatched orders. A one-sided SP pool pushes the clearing price off the continuous market, as closing-auction imbalances do in equities. This trader always lays at the SP, so any systematic gap is a cost on every bet.
nearest_known: Betfair's projected SP display and a public tutorial on predicting the BSP (betfair-datascientists.github.io/tutorials/analysingAndPredictingBSP); ledger hedge-ratio-1021. The step: a venue switch for the hedge leg driven by the pool's imbalance net of own orders.
novelty_check: One web search: BSP mechanics and the tutorial found; no study of near/far imbalance against the last traded price and no hedge-venue rule. Ledger scan for 'sp_near', 'far price': 0 hits.
first_test: Marks since 8 Oct: fit on the first half, test on the second; pass if the forecast gap's slope is positive at race-clustered t > 2.5 and the switch rule lowers the average lay price paid on the ledger's own backs (day bootstrap above zero).

title: Attention share of the day: ex-ante neglect of a race
one_line: Forecast each race's share of the day's exchange turnover before any money arrives and use neglect as a gate on how much to trust the morning price over the model.
definition: E_r = expected pre-off matched volume of race r: empirical-Bayes mean of total pp_vol by course x class band x race type x weekday x month (betfair_prices, days before today; shrink to the course mean, k = 20 races). a_r = E_r / sum of E over all UK/IE races that day; clash_r = number of races off within 10 minutes of r; rank_r = a_r's rank on the day. Features: -ln a_r, clash_r, rank_r, number of meetings that day. Model use: interact -ln a_r with both terms of the closing model (ln market now, ln model). Unseen course x class cells fall back to class x weekday.
data_needed: Held: betfair_prices volumes from 2018; the day's card.
card_time: From the 06:00 card and history.
mechanism: Traders and bots have finite capital and attention and price the day's main races first. A race expected to take a small share of the day stays near its tissue price longer and moves later, more so on days with many meetings - the distraction effect seen around busy earnings days in equities.
nearest_known: The closing model's realised-volume interactions (reports/race_book_model.md:32-35). The step: an ex-ante share of the day's attention, available before the book has traded, rather than the volume already seen.
novelty_check: One web search on busy-day or simultaneous-event effects in betting odds: nothing direct found (general under-reaction papers only).
first_test: Closing model refitted with the interaction on recorded marks; pass if the held-out error falls against the served closing model (race bootstrap) and the model weight rises with neglect.

title: Rival-avoidance index: field shortfall against eligible supply
one_line: A race's field-size shortfall against the supply of eligible horses measures how many rival yards stayed away - evidence that insiders rate one runner, often an unexposed one, above its public form.
definition: Walk-forward count model (negative-binomial boosted trees, earlier years only) of runners N per race on: course, month, weekday, race type, class, age/sex terms, rating band (max OR), trip, deflated prize, eligible supply (horses with a run in the last 90 days fitting code, age, sex, OR band, trip +-2f, with the course inside the yard's 90th-percentile travel km - bases as model/blocks/travel.py), and competing races of the same cell within 150 km and +-3 days. Shortfall S = (E[N] - N)/sqrt(E[N]); races at the safety limit are censored. Absentee share A = share of yards habitual in this cell at this course (3+ runners in 3 years) holding an eligible horse rested 7+ days that did not declare. Runner features: S, A, S x rank by mr_rating, S x unexposed (career_runs <= 3) x dm_stage_mkt, S x yard size. Cells with under 30 past races shrink to the class x type mean (k = 30).
data_needed: Held: race_results (runners, conditions, OR, trainer, dates), course coordinates in travel.py, market_rating block. Sharper with dated entries (entered but not declared) - not held (repo_data map section 3).

History holds runners only while the card includes later non-runners (351 of 5,932, ledger morning-card-gap-1110), so scale the card N by the yards' non-runner rates or accept a small bias.
mechanism: Trainers see entries, hear gallop talk and know which newcomers are rated at home; declaring against one is costly, so they wait for another race. Their joint absence is private information that surfaces only as a small field, which the card shows but nobody sets against supply. title: Conditions as a decoder: private valuations read from auction and claiming weights
one_line: In auction races the weight carried is set by sale price and in claimers by the trainer's own valuation, so past weights reveal point-in-time price bands without any sales file.
definition: Parse race_name for auction (not median), median auction, restricted/band, claiming, selling. (a) Auction maiden/novice: adjusted weight = card weight less the in-race sex allowance (estimated as the race's mean filly-colt gap) less penalties for earlier wins; price_band_lb = max adjusted weight in the race less the runner's (0 = dearest band). Stored on the horse from the next day as a static attribute. (b) Claimer: the same quantity is the valuation the trainer chose; features are its rank in today's claimer and, on later runs, the last self-valuation against the OR-implied one. (c) Eligibility bounds: a run in a median-auction or band-restricted race caps the sire median or price. Features: revealed_band (ordinal, NaN if never revealed), band against the field's revealed bands, share of field revealed, days since revealed, for unexposed runners band x yard (dm_). No allowance schedule is needed for the ordinal reading.
data_needed: Held: race_results race_name, pounds, claim, sex, earlier wins, from 2010. Optional: published race conditions to convert pounds to price steps (free, BHA/HRI programme; not held).

title: Roy-model inversion: private ability implied by the race chosen
one_line: Model each trainer's choice of race among the races the horse could have run in, then solve for the ability level that makes the chosen race the rational pick.
definition: Opportunity set O for a run on day d: races in [d-6, d] (plus forward days where the fixture list is held) admitting the horse by code, age and sex terms, class or rating band (band read from each race's runner OR range), maiden/novice status, trip within +-20% of its last three trips, course within the yard's 90th-percentile km. Step 1: conditional logit of the chosen race over O per trainer, coefficients shrunk to the pooled fit: log prize, class, km, trip less the horse's best trip, surface match, par level L of the race cell (trailing mean mr_field). Step 2: add theta x a x L and, with coefficients fixed, take the posterior mean of a for this horse-run under a normal prior (mr_rating, mr_sd). Features: gap = implied a less mr_rating, choice log-likelihood (surprise), number of alternatives, rank of the chosen race's par level and prize in O, count of easier and richer races passed over. O of size 1: NaN.
data_needed: Held: race_results calendar and conditions, travel.py yard bases, market_rating. Forward alternatives need the public fixture list and conditions (free: BHA and HRI; history not held, so start with the backward window).
card_time: Before 06:00: alternatives from results up to yesterday plus today's other cards; the choice model is fitted on earlier seasons.
mechanism: A trainer knows the horse's home work and picks the race maximising prize times chance less cost. Passing over easier or nearer races for a stronger one reveals a private estimate above the public one; the reverse reveals doubt. The card shows the race run, never the races declined, so the early price cannot use the comparison; stable money later does.
nearest_known: Class-move flags, tv_ travel against the yard's habit, connections.py schedule-expected strike rate. Roy self-selection models are standard in labour economics. Step beyond: an explicit opportunity set and a structural inversion to an ability estimate on the rating scale.

title: Cut-line pressure before oversubscribed handicaps
one_line: For horses near the rating needed to get a run in a big-field handicap, the distance to the expected cut says whether connections need a win now or need to protect the mark.

title: Variance premium: win share integrated over rating uncertainty
one_line: Replace the plug-in softmax of market ratings with the win share averaged over each runner's rating uncertainty, which lifts uncertain outsiders and trims uncertain favourites.
definition: Inputs per runner: mr_rating r_i and mr_sd s_i; unread horses take the field's mean rating and the block's initial sd (or dm_stage_mkt as the mean). Plug-in p = softmax(r). Integrated share q_i = E[softmax_i(r + e)], e_i ~ N(0, (kappa s_i)^2) independent - by 2,000 quasi-random draws, or to second order: q_i = p_i [1 + 0.5 (kappa s_i)^2 (1-p_i)(1-2p_i) + 0.5 sum_{j != i} (kappa s_j)^2 p_j (2p_j - 1)]. kappa is fitted on earlier folds by the likelihood of BSP shares (one value per race type), so it measures how the close itself prices uncertainty. Features: log(q/p) (variance premium), log(N q), the cross term alone (rivals' uncertainty), and the derivative of q_i in s_i. Fields under 3 rated runners: NaN.
data_needed: Held: market_rating block outputs (mr_rating, mr_sd), BSP history.
card_time: Before 06:00: ratings and sds as of yesterday, today's declared field.
mechanism: Win probability is convex in ability for outsiders and concave for strong favourites, so the same mean rating is worth more with a wide spread in a big field. mr_share ignores this, and a tree reading its own row cannot rebuild the cross-runner term. Unexposed horses are where the forecast error is largest (0.52 against 0.36 in handicaps, debut_market.py docstring).
nearest_known: mr_share (plug-in softmax), kr_ sd, Henery/Stern normal and gamma models with one common variance, TrueSkill's pairwise integration. Step beyond: runner-specific posterior variance pushed through the race softmax, with the market's own uncertainty scale kappa fitted.
novelty_check: One web search on heteroscedastic Thurstonian racing models: breeding rank models with fixed residual variance, a rider-specific variance model in endurance, Anderson 2015 (ideas.repec.org/a/taf/japsta/v42y2015i8p1740-1756.html) - no horse-specific-variance win probability found.
first_test: Compute q on the cached matrix (no rebuild). Compare log-loss of q against p on BSP shares out of fold, then screen the four features on 11 folds beside the market-rating candidate with a placebo. Pass: -0.0007 beyond the mr_ arm.

title: Debut-slot value from the yard's matured earlier cohorts
one_line: Rate each first run by how good the yard's earlier newcomers launched in the same kind of slot eventually became, not by how the market priced them on the day.
definition: Slot of a first run for trainer t = (course tier: quintile of the course's trailing 3-year mean mr_field in maiden/novice races; race type; month-of-season bucket; order of this newcomer in the yard's crop that season as a percentile; ridden by the yard's highest-share jockey or not, st_jk_share). Outcome for earlier newcomers: Y = mr_rating after the fifth run or 400 days after debut, whichever first, counted only once that date is before today. Slot value V(t, s) = decayed mean of Y (half-life 3 seasons) shrunk over 15 to the yard's all-newcomer mean, then to the slot's all-yard mean. Features: V; V as a z among the field's runners with three runs or fewer; V less dm_trc_debut_mkt (what the debut market gave that slot); on second and third runs, V at debut and today's slot value less the debut's (the yard's revised view).
data_needed: Held: race_results from 2010, market_rating (2018 on), stable/bookings jockey shares. Owner tier would add a slot dimension (owner only in blandford_results from 2021).
card_time: Before 06:00: slot attributes are on the card; Y uses only horses whose maturity date has passed.
mechanism: Large yards rank a crop at home and launch the better ones in particular maidens, months and under particular riders. The eventual ability of past occupants of a slot is a prior on today's newcomer. The debut market block measures the yard's average debut price; the slot's later truth is the part the early price misses and stable money supplies by the close.

title: Owner fingerprint: betting owners and crowd-owned horses
one_line: Measure each owner's history of morning-to-close price moves and classify owner type from the name, separating owners whose money is informed from syndicates whose money is loyal.
definition: Owner key: normalised owner string (titles stripped, partnership names sorted). Past-run move m = ln(morningwap/BSP). own_move = decayed mean of m (half-life 365 days) shrunk over 20 runs to the owner-type mean, then to the trainer's. Context versions: debut, handicap debut, 60+ days off, first run for the yard. Owner type by pattern: individual; partnership (2-4 names or '&'); syndicate or club (keywords syndicate, club, racing, partners, members); stud or breeder entity; large operation (40+ distinct runners a year). own_result = decayed shrunk mean of (won - BSP probability). Also owner x trainer cell, owner's share of its runs at today's course, and a flag when the race title contains the owner's or trainer's surname. Features are read as of the owner at the horse's most recent earlier run until the card's owner column is restored. Fewer than 5 runs: type mean only.

title: Jockey's forgone book: opportunity cost of today's rides
one_line: Value the rides a jockey gave up today from his regular yards against the ride he took, and mark the horses his choice passed over.
definition: Supplier yards of jockey j: yards where j took 15%+ of rides over the trailing 180 days (st_jk_share, decayed). Ride value v = mr_lshare of the horse in its race (fallback: OR-based share). Forgone set F: today's runners from supplier yards that j does not ride - at other meetings, or in the same race. Features for j's ride: v less the best v in F clashing within +-20 minutes or at another meeting (choice gap); sum of share x max(v, 0) over F (forgone value); number of rides at the meeting; km from j's base (centroid of his rides, as travel.py does for yards) against his usual. Mirror feature on a passed-over horse: 1 and the gap when a rider with 2+ of its last 3 rides is riding elsewhere today on a lower-v horse. Jockeys with under 100 rides in 365 days: NaN.
data_needed: Held: 06:00 cards for all meetings, race_results (jockey, trainer, dates), market_rating, travel.py coordinates.
card_time: Before 06:00: all meetings' declared riders are on the cards; shares and values from earlier days.
mechanism: A jockey and his agent choose among offers with what they know from riding work and from trainers. Taking a publicly weaker ride over a stronger one from a regular supplier reveals a private view, positive for the chosen horse and negative for the one left. The card lists each ride alone; the comparison across meetings is never shown, and the price learns it from money.

novelty_check: Repo maps: bookings and stable read the booked rider only, never the rides declined. No dedicated web search (budget); single-ride and jockey-switch angles are known practice, the forgone-book value was not found. Unverified beyond that.
first_test: Build on the 2018-2026 matrix (cards rebuilt from results). Screen on 11 folds beside bookings with a placebo; separately test the passed-over flag on ln(morningwap/BSP). Pass: -0.0007 beyond the bookings arm.

title: Campaign-state hidden Markov model of a horse's runs
one_line: Treat each horse's sequence of runs as a hidden campaign state - education, marking time, prep, target - inferred from the choices connections make, as ecologists infer animal behaviour from movement.
definition: One sequence per horse. Emissions known on the card for each run: log gap against the horse's usual, class change, trip less its best-rated trip, going fit, tv_km_vs_usual, bk_jk_upgrade, headgear change, log prize against its usual. Emission for past runs only: the market-rating surprise (reading less prior rating) and finish against market order. K states (start at 4, chosen by held-out predictive likelihood); transition matrix and emission means per trainer, shrunk to the pooled values (hierarchical, k = 50 runs). Fit by EM on earlier seasons. At 06:00: forward-filter to yesterday, then one step with today's card-known emissions only. Features: filtered state probabilities, expected surprise today given them, runs spent in the current non-target spell, and the trainer's decayed record against the price in each state. Horses with under 3 runs get the pooled prior.
data_needed: Held: race_results, travel, bookings, freshness and market_rating block outputs.
card_time: Before 06:00: today's choice emissions are all on the card; post-run emissions enter only for earlier days.
mechanism: Connections run a horse for different purposes on different days and signal it through a bundle of choices, none decisive alone. title: The race programme as a flow graph: prep and target roles of each race
one_line: Build a graph whose nodes are recurring races and whose edges are horses moving between them, and learn which races act as preps and which as targets.
definition: Node = recurring race slot: course, race type, class, trip band, age/sex terms, ISO week +-1, matched across years (name tokens after stripping sponsors help). Node statistics, shrunk to the class x type cell (k = 40 runners): prep_ness(u) = mean of (next-run surprise less this-run surprise) of past runners; target_ness(v) = mean surprise of arrivals; terminal share = share of past runners for whom it was the season's richest or last run. Edge lift(u, v) = mean surprise at v of arrivals from u less target_ness(v), shrunk k = 20. Features today: prep_ness and target_ness of today's node, lift of (last node, today), days to today's modal successor node, terminal share, and an 8-dimension spectral embedding of the node in the flow graph.

card_time: Before 06:00: today's node from the card; all statistics from earlier seasons.
mechanism: Trainers use the programme as routes: some races are stepping stones where horses run below what the market expects and improve next time, others are destinations. title: Phase-resolved jockey skill matched to the horse's own deficit
