title: Desk drift and pool exchange rates for official marks
one_line: Treat the unit of an official mark as varying between handicapping desks, regions and time, estimate exchange rates from horses that cross pools, and detect when a desk's habits change.
definition: Pools: jurisdiction (GB, IE) x code x trip band x surface x region (north/south by course latitude). Well-in of a handicap run w = log(N x BSP share) less its class-cell mean - in a handicap the price is the market's disagreement with the mark. (a) Exchange rate: for horses whose consecutive handicap runs cross from pool A to B within 120 days, y = w at B less w at A; x_AB(t) = Kalman-smoothed mean of y, shrunk to 0 over 50 crossings. (b) Drift: per pool and month, mean w of horses on their first run after a re-mark, and the mean residual of the shadow-handicapper reaction model; a CUSUM or Bayesian change-point test flags a break and the state is the posterior mean since the last break. Features: x_AB on a mover's first three runs in the new pool; pool drift state; flag that the horse was re-marked after the last break and has not run since; days since the break.
data_needed: Held: race_results (OR, class, course, dates), BSP history, travel.py coordinates. Public desk assignments would sharpen the pools (not held).
card_time: Before 06:00: pools from the card; rates and states from earlier days.
mechanism: Marks are set by different people for different populations and their habits shift when staff or policy change. A horse moving pools, or re-marked under a new regime, carries a mark whose value the market has to re-learn from results; until it has, early prices lean on the number as printed. Remarkable if true: the drift would be a slow, tradable regime.

title: Martingale-exact percentile of in-running price extremes
one_line: Turn each past run's in-play low (or high, for winners) into the exact probability of seeing that extreme given its BSP, a starting-price-neutral score of how the horse really travelled.
definition: Inputs held: betfair_prices bsp, ipmin, ipmax, ip_vol, win_lose. p0 = race-normalised 1/BSP. Loser: m = min(1/ipmin, 0.99); for a continuous martingale absorbed at 0/1, P(max >= m | loses) = p0(1-m) / (m(1-p0)) = u. Winner: l = 1/ipmax; P(min <= l | wins) = l(1-p0) / ((1-l)p0) = v. Scores s = -ln u, w = -ln v (Exp(1) under the null, whatever the BSP). Second step, because prices jump and long-odds ladders are thin: re-rank s within BSP decile x in-play volume band x run-style class on earlier days only (probability integral transform). Race level: S = sum_i 1/ipmin_i (how many horses looked like winning). Features: windows l1, m3, w5, career of s; w for last win (how nearly it lost); S of the last race; beaten runs with s in the top decile. NaN when ip_vol below a floor or no record; ipmin >= BSP gives u = 1.
data_needed: Held: betfair_prices (2018-2026, ledger open-close-inventory-1101).
card_time: Past runs only; price files lag one day, so yesterday's runs enter a day late.
mechanism: ir_lowr (log low/BSP) mixes how well a horse travelled with how short it started: a 2.0 shot cannot halve as a 20.0 shot can. The percentile strips the starting price out exactly. In-play traders saw the run; a tissue built from finishing positions did not, so the price is corrected by later money.

title: The handicapper as a sensor: reaction-function residual of the mark
one_line: Fit how the official handicapper normally changes a mark given the bare result, and use what he did beyond that as his private reading of the hidden race.
definition: Inputs held: race_results OR per run, today's card OR, position, distbt, class, field, race type. For run r: dOR = next published mark - mark at r (for the last run: today's card OR - OR then). Fit g = E[dOR | finishing position, lb beaten, performance figure - mark, win margin, class, field size, handicap flag, age, code, days to next run, leave-one-out mean dOR of the race's other runners] by monotone GBDT on seasons before the fold. Residual h = dOR - g. Features: hr_l1, hr_m3; hr_race_l1 (mean h of the other runners of its last race, shrunk by 4); hr_silent (mark change with no run in between); hr_open (first handicap mark - mean of its figures). GB and IE fitted apart; penalties excluded; gaps over 120 days dropped. Identifying assumption: given g's covariates, h is the handicapper's judgement, not an omitted public variable - checked with a placebo residual from a mis-specified g.

card_time: Card OR is known at 06:00; all else from earlier days.
mechanism: The handicapper watches every race and publishes one number. The part of his change the result cannot explain is an expert's view of eased, unlucky or flattered runs. It is read as weight, not as information; sharper money that watched the replay agrees with him after the tissue is set.

title: Stale-mark news: two-vintage differencing keyed to the horse's last trade
one_line: Compute the forecast twice - on what was known just after the horse last ran and on what is known now - and give the difference, the never-traded news, its own weight in the closing model.
definition: For each runner, t0 = day of its last run (its last full-liquidity price). Build the lag-safe inputs at two vintages: A = as of t0+1 (own last run included), B = as of today 06:00. title: Effective resistance of the form graph as a knowability gate
one_line: Measure, by electrical resistance through the whole who-met-whom graph, how precisely public form can compare each runner with its rivals, and let that set how far the morning price should be trusted.
definition: Graph at day t: nodes = horses with a run in 730 days; edge weight w_ij = sum over shared races of exp(-age/365) x q, q = 1 if both finished within 20 lb of the winner else 0.3. Laplacian L. For today's field F, R_ij = (e_i - e_j)' L+ (e_i - e_j), solved by conjugate gradient on the 3-step neighbourhood. In a least-squares rating Var(r_i - r_j) = s2 R_ij exactly. Features: er_mean (mean R to rivals), er_min, er_rank, er_field (mean pairwise R), er_disc (share of pairs with no path; R capped at the 99th percentile; newcomers at the cap). Use: columns for the forecaster, and an interaction in the closing model on (ln model - ln morning) and on the simulated move variance (model/race_book.py Monte Carlo band).
data_needed: Held: race_results (who met whom, margins).
card_time: Graph from earlier days; today's field from the 06:00 card.
mechanism: Where the graph ties a field tightly, anyone can price it and the morning price is near final. Where resistance is high the tissue is guesswork, private knowledge decides, and moves are larger. It says when the model or the morning price deserves weight, which volume bands only proxy.
nearest_known: cl_rivals / cl_links counts (collateral), mr_read_share, mr_sd. Theory: Hendrickx et al. 2019 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/hendrickx19a.html), Chen 2023 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06821). Step: exact comparison variance through all paths, used as a trust gate.
novelty_check: Web search for effective resistance with racing or collateral form: theory papers only, no racing use.

title: Conditional surprisal of the in-running comment given the bare result
one_line: Score each past comment by how improbable its wording is given where the horse finished, and in which direction, with the race-reader's style removed.
definition: Inputs held: race_results comment (from 2012), position, distbt, field, BSP, track, date. Split comments into clauses, map to canonical phrase ids (top ~3,000). Context c = finish-percentile bucket, lengths-beaten bucket, BSP bucket, race type, trip band, writer cluster. Writer cluster: k-means (K ~ 30) on clause tf-idf vectors per course-day (one race-reader a meeting). Model q(clause_k | clause_k-1, c): smoothed bigram, fitted on years before the fold. Surprisal S = -(1/n) sum log q. Direction D = E[finish percentile | clauses] (ridge on clause indicators + cluster, earlier years) - actual percentile. card_time: Past runs' comments only; models fitted on earlier years.
mechanism: A comment predictable from the result adds nothing to the figure; one improbable given the result ('led, clear, eased' on a fifth) is where the figure misleads. title: Pool exchange rates: priced versus realised offsets across form circuits
one_line: Find the loosely connected pools of horses, estimate from bridge horses only the offset between pools in market terms and in result terms, and feed the gap as the market's exchange-rate error.
definition: Pools: communities of the co-race graph on a trailing 365 days (Leiden or a degree-corrected block model, K 8-12), labelled by country, code, surface, region. Two currencies: market readings (mr_) and result figures (the kr_ performance figure). For each ordered pool pair (a,b) and month: dM_ab = mean over horses crossing a->b of (market reading in b - market rating carried from a); dR_ab the same with figures less Kalman rating. Monthly local-level smoothing; shrink to 0 with k = 50 bridge runs. Runner whose rating precision was mostly earned in a, in a field mostly of b: xr_mkt = dM_ab, xr_res = dR_ab, xr_gap = dR - dM, xr_n (bridge runs), xr_first (first crossing). Same-pool runners: 0.
data_needed: Held: race_results, BSPs, performance figures.
card_time: Pools and offsets from earlier days; field composition from the 06:00 card.
mechanism: Ratings in two pools are comparable only through the few horses that cross. The market sets the cross rate by reputation. A realised rate that differs is a mispricing with a few dozen parameters and thousands of bridge runs - estimable, unlike horse or yard residuals, which did not persist (L:iter11-ae).

novelty_check: Not web-searched (budget). Raiders' records exist as trainer tables in practice; no bridge-estimated rate on the maps. Unverified.

title: Per-horse critical speed and reserve fitted from race times
one_line: Fit each horse the endurance-physiology curve distance = critical speed x time + reserve from its own runs at different trips, with family priors, to price a change of trip in pounds.
definition: Inputs held: comptime, total_dst_bt, distance yards, rail_move, pounds, going; day allowance from time_figure; pace flags from timeform_pace. Own time T = winner's time + lengths x 2.4 m / finishing speed; T* = T less the day's going allowance. Model D = CS_i x T* + Dp_i; weight scales CS by (1 - k (lb - ref)). Hierarchy: CS_i, Dp_i ~ Normal(cohort mean by age, sex, code + sire effect, tau). Truly run races (race finishing speed within the par band, or time within a margin of standard) enter as equalities; slowly run races as one-sided bounds (the horse could have gone at least this fast). Fit by EM on days before t. Features: predicted time at today's trip as race z, gap, rank; stamina index Dp/CS; predicted lb gain or loss for today's trip vs last; posterior sds. Fewer than 2 trips -> sire/cohort prior. Flat first; jumps need a per-obstacle term.

card_time: Past runs only; today's trip from the card.
mechanism: Figures rate a run at the trip it was run; the market carries a rating to a new trip by pedigree and feel. A two-parameter curve identified from the horse's own runs says what the change is worth for this horse. The tissue seldom moves a rating for trip; the stamina money comes later.

title: Kin-pooled within-horse response slopes, priced versus realised
one_line: For a first try at a trip, ground or obstacle, borrow relatives' within-horse responses to that change - never their levels - once as the market priced them and once as they ran.

title: Reappearance-hazard residuals: own return surprise and rivals' excess absence
one_line: Model when a horse like this, after a run like that, normally runs again; score how late or early it has come back, and how many of its last race's rivals have failed to reappear.

Fitted on earlier years. Own: Cox-Snell residual r = cumulative hazard at the actual gap; ret_surp = log r (high = back much later than expected). title: Twin causal forests for condition changes with a programme-scarcity instrument
one_line: Learn which horses truly respond to a change of trip, surface or class, and how the market prices that response, using changes forced by a thin race programme as the natural experiment.
definition: Treatment W: trip up or down 2f+, surface switch, class drop (headgear without instrument, flagged weaker). Outcomes: Y_M = today's market reading - rating before; Y_R = performance figure - Kalman rating. Instrument Z: for the horse's eligibility (mark band, age, sex, code), the count of races at its usual trip and surface within 150 km of the yard base (tv_ coordinates) in the 21 days around the run, from the record of races run. Covariates X: finishing-speed profile, stride length where held, run style, kin priors, age, yard's propensity to change. Instrumental forests, cross-fitted by year, give tau_R(x), tau_M(x). Features: te_real, te_priced, te_gap, te_se. Identifying assumption: scarcity shifts the choice but is unrelated to the horse's private fitness or response (exclusion), and monotone; abandoned fixtures are missing from the record, which biases Z slightly.

card_time: Forests fitted on earlier years; today's X and W from the 06:00 card.
mechanism: A trainer usually changes trip because he knows something, so before/after comparisons are confounded. When the calendar forces the change, the response is the horse's own aptitude. The market prices changes by yard reputation and pedigree; an individual, unconfounded prediction may differ.

title: Reason-split closing combine: TreeSHAP families inside the market blend
one_line: Split our forecast's log-odds into a dozen feature-family contributions and let the closing model give each its own weight beside the morning price, learning which of our reasons the close confirms.
definition: For each runner take LightGBM pred_contrib from the main member (target: logit of race-normalised share), out-of-fold only. Centre each family sum within the race: c_if. Closing logit u_i = a*lq_market_i + sum_f b_f*c_if + the present volume and depth terms; q = race softmax; fitted by cross-entropy to the BSP book exactly as now (model/race_book.py:110-143). b_f = b + d_f with a ridge penalty on d_f (lambda chosen walk-forward); d_f = 0 for all f recovers today's model, so it nests the served one. title: Conditions-aware low-rank market rating from past Betfair SPs
one_line: Turn the scalar market rating into a horse vector times a learned conditions embedding, so past prices say what the market thinks of this horse at this trip, ground and track type.
definition: Replace r_i in model/blocks/market_rating.py with r_i(x) = a_i + v_i . g(x). x = conditions (log trip, going scale, surface, course-shape class, field band, class); g(x) = sum of per-attribute embeddings, K = 3 or 4 dimensions; v_i = horse loading with prior N(V_sire + V_trainer, S). Reading equation unchanged: y_i = log p_i + C_i, rivals' ratings evaluated at that race's x. Fit in two alternating steps on races before 2021 (as FIT_UNTIL): (1) g, V_sire, V_trainer by gradient steps on the one-step predictive likelihood of BSP readings; (2) per-horse Kalman filter on the state (a_i, v_i) with observation row [1, g(x)]. Features: rating at today's x, its sd (larger when today's x is far from where the horse has been priced), the aptitude part v_i . g(x_today), softmax share, gap, z. Under 3 readings v_i stays at its prior.
data_needed: Held: race_results.bfsp with trip, going, surface, track, class, sire, trainer, 2010 on (repo_data map).

title: Nested substitution at withdrawal against Betfair's proportional reduction
one_line: Fit a nested logit to closing books so we know which remaining runners gain more than Betfair's proportional cut when a rival comes out, and price that into the morning entry bar.
definition: Two-level nested logit on the BSP book. Nests: projected pace role (leader / prominent / held up), draw third on straight courses, same yard. Share_i = P(nest) * P(i | nest), dissimilarity lambda_n in (0,1]. Fitted without non-runner history: IIA says log BSP share minus log softmax of market-rating strengths is unrelated to nest composition; estimate lambda by cross-entropy on BSP books, walk-forward. For a withdrawal of j: nested ratio_ij = share_i without j / with j; proportional ratio = 1/(1 - p_j). Feature nr_gain_i = sum_j P(NR_j) * [log nested ratio_ij - log proportional ratio], plus free mass = sum_j P(NR_j) * p_j * 1[p_j < 2.5%] (Betfair applies no win-market reduction under 2.5% per a trading-software help page - re-check Betfair's rules). P(NR_j) from card-versus-result records by trainer, going change, stall. Entry bar: expected CLV after the expected reduction plus nr_gain.
data_needed: Held: BSP 2018 on, pace engine roles, mr_ ratings; live marks with adjustment factor and removal time from 30 Sep 2026; 06:00 cards from 14 Jul 2026 for non-runner rates (race_results holds no non-runners).
card_time: lambda and P(NR) from earlier days; nests from the 06:00 card. The realised removal is used only for validation.
mechanism: A matched back is cut by one factor for all, but a withdrawn front-runner hands the lead to the other pace horses and a withdrawn stablemate concentrates the yard's money. Reductions take the trader's edge from +5.66% to +1.76% (L:reductions-1021), so the part of the true move that the cut does not match is real money either way.

novelty_check: Web search (nested logit, IIA, Rule 4, reduction factor): only bookmaker and exchange guides; no formal treatment found.
first_test: (a) 2021 on: does nest composition explain log BSP share minus log mr softmax share out of sample (cross-entropy gain, race-bootstrap interval above zero). (b) Live record: in races with a removal after 10:00, regress survivors' log(BSP share x (1 - p_j) / pre-removal share) on the predicted non-proportional term. Pass: slope above zero, 90% interval.

title: Market-implied volatility per horse from prices across field compositions
one_line: Read each closing book as a Thurstonian race with horse-specific variance, inferring each horse's variance from how its price share changes with field size and strength.
definition: Performance X_i ~ N(mu_i, sigma_i^2); share_i = P(X_i is the maximum) = integral of phi_i(x) * prod_{j != i} Phi((x - mu_j)/sigma_j), by Gauss-Hermite quadrature. log sigma_i = gamma . z_i + h_i; z_i = exposure (readings, age, code, first time at trip/going), h_i a horse effect shrunk to zero. Identification: a high-variance horse keeps its share in big, strong fields and loses it in small, weak ones, relative to softmax. Fit: mu from the existing market-rating readings; gamma on books before 2021 by cross-entropy to BSP shares; h_i by a slow filter. Features: mv_sigma, the Thurstonian share today, its log ratio to mr_share, and the second-order terms 0.5*sigma_i^2*p_i(1-p_i)(1-2p_i) (own) and sum_j 0.5*sigma_j^2*p_i*p_j(2p_j-1) (rivals'). Optional second identifier: the horse's lagged residual of bfsp_place against the win-implied place price.
data_needed: Held: race_results.bfsp, bfsp_place, field sizes; mr_ readings.
card_time: sigma and mu from earlier days; today's field from the 06:00 card.
mechanism: A softmax of point ratings gives the same share to a solid horse and an erratic one; the close does not, and it prices unexposed horses with their upside, more so in big fields. The forecast is compressed 5-7% against the BSP, a long-shot effect, and a global stretch failed on Brier (L:within-race-stretch). A variance-aware share addresses the compression where it arises.

title: Yard informedness from the price-performance lead-lag area
one_line: Measure, yard by yard, whether its horses' prices move before their performances change or only after, and use that to decide when a morning price that disagrees with us is information.
definition: Per horse, a 2-D path over runs k: x_k = the market reading before run k (market_rating's y), y_k = the performance figure of run k, both standardised by pool. Level-2 signature antisymmetric term A = 0.5 * sum_{j<k} (dx_j*dy_k - dy_j*dx_k). Split it: anticipation c_ant = sum_k dx_k*dy_k (price moved before the run that showed the change); follow c_fol = sum_k dy_k*dx_{k+1}. Pool over a yard's horses, 730 days back, half-life 365 days: yard_inf = (c_ant - c_fol) / (|c_ant| + |c_fol| + k), k fitted, shrunk to the pool mean; also by yard x (two-year-old, handicap debut, after 100+ days off). Uses: (i) forecast feature, alone and times mr_surprise; (ii) closing model term (lq_market - lq_model) * yard_inf. Yards under 40 horse-runs get the pool value.

card_time: From runs before today. The closing interaction uses the morning price at entry time only.
mechanism: In some yards the price moves before the improvement shows - their money knows. For those, a morning price away from our form forecast is information and the close goes further; for yards whose prices only follow form, it is noise and the close returns to the forecast. The gap term alone added nothing (L:closing-model-v2-0930) because it pools both kinds.

title: Bornhuetter-Ferguson franking: chain-ladder development of form lines
one_line: Treat each past race as an insurance cohort whose franking arrives over time, and project its ultimate worth from what has developed so far plus a prior.
definition: Mapping: accident period = past race R; claims = franking received, the sum over R's other runners' later runs of (change in market rating since R) or (win - BSP chance); development age t = days since R. Build development triangles over all earlier races by cell (code x class x field band): D(t) = share of the 180-day franking seen by age t. Prior ultimate P_R = cell mean given R's field level (mr_field). Estimate U_R = F_R(t) + (1 - D(t)) * P_R (Bornhuetter-Ferguson); chain-ladder F_R(t)/D(t) once D(t) > 0.5. Features per horse: U of the last race and of the last three (the horse's own runs excluded), D(t), and the newest increment - franking that arrived in the last 7 days. Rivals who never reappear count as undeveloped, not zero.
data_needed: Held: race_results, mr_ ratings.
card_time: Triangles and franking from days before today.
mechanism: The worth of a horse's last race keeps arriving as its rivals run again. Today's features take the franking seen so far at face value, so the most recent races - the ones that matter most - read as thin samples. The newest increment (a rival won two days ago) is least likely to be in ratings-based morning prices and is known to the closing crowd.

title: Race-load fitness-fatigue impulse response per horse and yard
one_line: Transplant the Banister training model: every past race adds fitness and fatigue that decay at different rates, fitted to how the close re-prices horses.
definition: readiness_i(t) = k1 * sum_s w_s * exp(-(t-s)/tau1) - k2 * sum_s w_s * exp(-(t-s)/tau2), over the horse's earlier runs s. Race load w_s = furlongs x going-effort factor x (1 + closeness of finish) x weight factor, standardised by code; an eased or pulled-up run gets a reduced load. Parameters by code and age band with trainer random effects on k1 and k2 (shrunk), fitted by least squares on (a) the next market-rating innovation (reading less rating before) and (b) log(morningwap/BSP). Grids: tau1 20-60 days, tau2 3-15 days. Features: fitness term, fatigue term, net, days until the net peaks, each with its race z. After 200+ days off the fitness term is at its floor and the trainer's first-run effect stands in.

card_time: From earlier runs and today's date.
mechanism: A hard recent race leaves fitness and fatigue; fatigue fades faster. title: Race-coupled forecast uncertainty through the softmax Jacobian
one_line: Model each runner's rating uncertainty, then propagate it across the field in closed form, so we know when a rival we cannot rate makes every price in the race unreliable.

title: One market-taught relevance kernel reused for every windowed feature
one_line: Learn from past prices how fast a run's relevance fades with days, trip, ground and class differences, then weight every form measure by that single kernel instead of run-count windows.
definition: In the market-rating filter let a reading from run s inform today t with variance R * exp(d(s,t)), d = th_trip*|dlog trip| + th_going*|dgoing| + th_surface*1[differs] + th_code*1[differs] + th_class*|dclass| + th_time*(days/365), all th >= 0, fitted by the one-step predictive likelihood of BSP readings before 2021. Recompute each per-run measure of form_windows (figure, pounds beaten, NFP, A-E and the rest of the 11) as sum_s w*m_s / sum_s w, with effective n = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2, shrunk to the horse's unweighted mean by n_eff/(n_eff + k). title: Stochastic frontier rating: ability as a frontier with one-sided shortfalls
one_line: Transplant stochastic frontier analysis: a run equals ability minus a one-sided shortfall plus noise, so ability is a frontier and the expected shortfall today is forecast separately.
definition: Mapping: output = performance figure of run k (pounds scale); frontier = ability a_i(t), a local level with an age term; composed error = v - u, v ~ N(0, s_v^2), u >= 0 half-normal with scale s_u * exp(delta . z_k) (Battese-Coelli determinants). z_k: trip and going distance from the horse's best, days off, field size, trouble flag from the comment, class rise, first-time headgear, trainer effect. delta, s_u, s_v by maximum likelihood pooled by code on runs before 2021; a_i by a filter with the skew-normal likelihood (moment-matched updates). Features: frontier a_i and its sd; E[u | z_today]; a_i - E[u]; P(u < 3 lb today); frontier less the Kalman mean; race z of each. Horses with one run: the frontier equals the cell prior plus that run's upside only.
data_needed: Held: performance figures, conditions, comments.
card_time: Filter from earlier runs; z_today from the 06:00 card.
mechanism: A horse can run below its ability for many reasons and above it for almost none. A symmetric filter splits the difference (the Kalman block added nothing alone, L:iter96). The market rates a horse nearer its best with excuses for the rest; the frontier is that reading made exact, and the forecast shortfall is the will-it-run-to-it part.
nearest_known: The Kalman rating, best-of figures in the exposure block, tanh-truncated margins. Step: a one-sided error whose size is modelled from the run's circumstances.
novelty_check: Web search (stochastic frontier + horse racing rating): no racing use found; nearest is a hierarchical horse-and-jockey panel model.
first_test: Paired screen: frontier features against kr_ features in predicting next-run log BSP share; then the 11-fold block screen. Pass under the noise bar with interval excluding zero.

title: Temporal graph memory network trained on closing books
one_line: Give every horse, trainer, jockey and sire a learned memory that is updated after each race by its own run and its rivals' memories, trained to predict closing prices.
definition: Nodes: horses, trainers, jockeys, sires, each with a 32-dimension memory. title: Attrition dividend: a cure-model share for jump races
one_line: Price each jumper as completion times winning among the completers, with rivals' fall risks and a shared race shock inside the share, not just the horse's own fall rate.
definition: Generative story: runner j completes with probability c_j = exp(-Z * h_j * n_obs); h_j = per-obstacle hazard from a logistic model on the horse's fall/unseat/pulled-up record (jf_), first time over the obstacle, jockey, field size, going; n_obs approximated from trip and code; Z ~ Gamma(1/phi, phi) a race frailty shared by all runners. Given the completer set S the winner is drawn by softmax of strengths s (mr_ ratings) over S. Share_i = E_Z E_S[1(i in S) * exp(s_i) / sum_{k in S} exp(s_k)], by 2,000 draws or a second-order expansion. Fit h on non-completions in race_results; phi from the over-dispersion of non-completions per race. Features: c_i, attrition dividend = log(share_i / softmax share_i), expected completers, P(the top-rated rival fails to complete).
data_needed: Held: race_results placing codes and comments for non-completions, mr_ ratings. Obstacle counts per course: free public course guides, or the trip proxy.
card_time: Hazards from earlier days; field from the 06:00 card.
mechanism: A sound jumper's chance rises when fragile rivals are short in the betting; a softmax of ratings with the horse's own fall rate misses the rivals' side and the shared shock. A UK study links fall risk to field size (madbarn summary of 10,866 starts). The close prices this; a ratings-based 06:00 forecast does not.

title: Innovation-form member: model the change since the horse was last priced
one_line: Add a member whose target is today's price reading minus the horse's market rating, fed every input as its change since the previous run, removing the horse's fixed quality.
definition: Target d_i = y_i - mr_rating_i, where y_i is today's market reading (log BSP share plus race level, as market_rating defines it) and mr_rating the rating before today. Features: each served per-horse input differenced against its value as of the horse's previous run (class, trip, going, jockey's market standing, weight against the field, yard form, field strength mr_field, mark), plus the last run's news (margin, figure, in-play low, days since) and the franking since. Fit one LightGBM member on d; forecast share = race softmax of (mr_rating + d_hat); blend through the existing gate. Horses with no reading are left to the three served members.

card_time: Differences use the previous run's stored values and the 06:00 card.
mechanism: A horse's unobserved quality is already in its past prices; level features spend trees re-learning it. Differencing is the panel within-estimator: it removes the horse effect and leaves the one question the morning market also has to answer - what has changed since this horse was last priced.

title: Error twins: an analog ensemble in the forecast's own leaf space
one_line: For each runner find past runners the model treated the same way and that the morning price disagreed with similarly, and read how the close resolved those disagreements.
definition: Embed each runner by its leaf indices in the main member (pred_leaf); similarity = share of trees in which two runners fall in the same leaf. At entry time take the 200 most similar out-of-fold runners from earlier days whose morning price sat on the same side of our forecast with a log gap within 0.15 of today's. Features: the twins' mean log(BSP / morning price); the share of twins whose close moved toward our forecast; mean similarity (low = the runner is unlike the training data); the twins' mean absolute forecast error. Used as closing-model inputs and as a veto when similarity is low. Fewer than 50 twins: features missing.
data_needed: Held: out-of-fold forecasts and leaf indices, betfair_prices.morningwap and bsp 2018 on.
card_time: Later-morning feature (needs the morning price at entry). Twins come from strictly earlier days, so no price of today enters their outcomes.
mechanism: A linear blend gives one answer to every disagreement of a given size. Twins give a local record: in this corner of feature space, when the market said shorter than us, who was right. Mean similarity doubles as a native measure of extrapolation.

title: Amortised Bayesian handicapper trained on simulated careers
one_line: Train a network on millions of simulated races drawn from a prior matched to the real record, so one forward pass returns the posterior win shares for a real field's histories.
definition: Generative prior for careers: ability as a random walk with an age curve; aptitude loadings over trip and going; one-sided shortfalls (idea 11); yard effects; fields assembled by class; results by a Thurstonian draw; prices = true shares plus noise. Hyperparameters are tuned so simulated summaries (margin distributions, repeat-winner rates, price dispersion by field size) match the held record, by the ABC machinery of model/abm/calibrate.py. Train a set-of-sequences transformer (tokens = each runner's past runs; attention across runners) on the order of 10^7 simulated races to output each runner's posterior win share from observable histories only - a prior-data fitted network. At 06:00 feed the real field's histories; outputs: share, entropy, penultimate embedding, used as features. Optional fine-tune of the last layers on BSP books before 2021.
data_needed: Held data for matching the prior and for the test. Needs a GPU training job; not runnable under this machine's limits.
card_time: Inputs are past-run histories to yesterday and the 06:00 card.
mechanism: With sparse evidence of unequal quality, how to weigh runs is a Bayesian computation; trees approximate it through about 1,000 hand summaries. A prior-fitted network learns the exact posterior for the assumed world, including fields of unexposed horses. It only helps if the prior is close to reality - that is the risk.

novelty_check: Relies on the adjacent map (tabular foundation models and neural posterior estimation: none found for racing). Not re-searched.

title: Market-implied going gap traded as a meeting basket
one_line: Invert the morning price cross-section for the going the market is assuming, compare it with a weather-model going forecast, and back the going-sensitive runners on the side of the gap.
definition: Per runner, going sensitivity b_i = slope of the horse's past race-normalised log BSP share (net of its market rating) on the going scale, shrunk to sire and damsire (k fitted). Per meeting at 06:00, implied shift g_m = slope, across the meeting's runners with race fixed effects, of (ln morning exchange share - ln served forecast share) on b_i. Forecast shift f_m = soil-water-balance going at off time from forecast rain and evapotranspiration (mean of 3+ weather models and their previous runs) minus the card's going, with sd s_m from the model and lead-time spread. Gap D_m = f_m - g_m. Position: back runners with b_i x D_m > 0, stake proportional to |b_i x D_m| / s_m, capped as the live rule, one side per race; lay at SP. Skip meetings with |D_m| under one sd or fewer than 20 runners with b_i known.
data_needed: Held: race_results going and bfsp 2010+, betfair_prices morningwap 2018+, live marks from 30 Sep 2026, 06:00 cards from 14 Jul 2026. Free public: Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API (2022+) and Previous Runs API (Jan 2024+), data CC BY 4.0 per its home page (open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-forecast-api, /previous-runs-api); ensemble members are not archived there. Realised rain: reanalysis archive (free).

mechanism: The 06:00 book is thin and anchored on the card's going; 27% of runners race on a going different from the morning card (L:card-vs-results-1110). Weather models already hold the rain to come; clerks update later and afternoon money re-prices going-dependent horses together. The price cross-section shows how much the market already holds; only the gap is traded, so a forecast everyone has read shows as D near zero and earns nothing.

title: Runner-level removal carry with unequal inheritance of a withdrawn rival
one_line: Value each morning back by what it gains when each rival is withdrawn - who inherits the chance - less Betfair's posted cut, weighted by a runner-level withdrawal hazard.
definition: For runner i at entry: V_i = sum over rivals j of h_j x (s_ij - c_j). h_j = chance j is withdrawn after now: logit on the trainer's shrunk withdrawal rate, j also declared tomorrow (48-hour declarations), going moved against j, price drift since the evening book, reserve status, hours to off. c_j = Betfair's adjustment factor shown in the book if at least 2.5%, else 0. s_ij = expected fractional shortening of i if j goes = p_j/(1 - p_j) x k_ij, with k_ij (probability-weighted mean 1 across survivors) from a kernel fitted on recorded removals: same run style, neighbouring stall, same price band, same yard, favourite removed. Entry bar: expected CLV + V_i >= 3%; stake as the rule. Edge cases: cuts cap at 90%; k shrunk to 1 where a cell has under 200 removals; place markets cut at any factor.

Longer removal history: Betfair Historic BASIC market definitions Jan 2024+, if the raw files are kept (not confirmed).
card_time: h_j, c_j, p_j from the 06:00 card, tomorrow's declarations and the book at entry; recomputed at each decision to 10:00.
mechanism: Betfair cuts every matched back by one posted factor, proportional across survivors, and not at all under 2.5%. The real transfer is unequal: a withdrawn pace rival or stablemate hands its chance to particular runners. The ledger finds the factor fair on average (11.20% against 10.97% of the book) and small removals free (+3.03% to the others) (L:removal-by-market-1109). The lay at SP is not cut, so the runner-level spread is collected by whoever holds the right backs.

title: Bridge-pinned resting backs priced off the forecast close
one_line: Place resting morning backs at the level that maximises expected profit when the price path is a bridge from now to the closing model's forecast, charging adverse selection exactly.
definition: Model the log price from now (x0) to the off as a Brownian path with integrated variance S (by hours to off and price band, from recorded marks and stream) and terminal law N(mu, tau^2) from the closing model. For a resting back at level m > x0, the chance the path touches m given a close c is 1 if c >= m, else exp(-2 (m - x0)(m - c) / S) (maximum of a Brownian bridge). Expected CLV per unit at m = integral over c of P(touch | c) x (exp(m - c) - 1) x N(c; mu, tau^2); fills are likelier when the close is high, so adverse selection is inside the integral. Post resting backs at the m maximising it, sized as the rule; a fill counts only when traded volume at m exceeds the queue ahead; cancel 15 minutes before the off; unfilled stake falls back to the live rule at 09:45.
data_needed: Held: betfair_live_marks from 30 Sep 2026 (300 s polls); Exchange Stream full and traded ladder, first morning 12 Nov 2026 (research/horse_stream_record.py); the closing book Monte Carlo (model/race_book.py:164).
card_time: Levels solved at 06:00 from the forecast and first book; re-solved at each poll to 10:00.
mechanism: Every position closes in a guaranteed auction at a known time, so the right fill model is the path's maximum conditional on where the model says it ends, not a forward fill model. Morning books are thin (median GBP1,423 matched at 08:00, repo_data map citing L:open-close-inventory-1101), so paths overshoot to levels the best back never shows at a poll, and a patient order is paid for supplying that liquidity.
nearest_known: Paper desk quotes at closing-model fair +-3% (L:paper-desk-1104); football resting orders against the recorded queue; finance fill-probability models. Step: the level is set by the bridge maximum pinned on the forecast close. Exit-side take-profits are excluded: they lost (L:arms-full-1103).

first_test: On stream days from 12 Nov: check calibration of P(touch) by decile, then replay the rule's runners with bridge-level resting backs against the traded ladder; baseline the live rule's fills on the same runners and days. Pass (registered first): CLV x stake a day after cuts higher, 90% day-bootstrap interval of the difference above zero on 30+ days, deflated Sharpe >= 0.95.

title: Yard-base training interruption index from reanalysis weather
one_line: Weather at the training yard, not the course, in the weeks before the race - frost, snow, waterlogging, heat - as a dated, exogenous shock to preparation that leads the yard's form.
definition: Geocode each yard (public trainer directory address; fallback the travel block's centroid). From hourly reanalysis at that point, over the 7, 14 and 28 days to yesterday: hours with 0-7 cm soil temperature below 0 C, snow-depth days, days with rain over 10 mm, heat-stress hours (temperature-humidity index over a fitted threshold), each as an anomaly against the yard's own 10-year norm for that calendar week. I = fitted non-negative combination. Runner features: I at its yard; I minus the field mean; I x days since last run (a recent race substitutes for gallops); I x unraced or returning; yard-specific sensitivity by empirical Bayes (stands in for an unknown all-weather gallop). Region index = mean I over yards within 15 km (shared gallops).
data_needed: Held: race_results trainer and dates; course coordinates and yard centroids in model/blocks/travel.py. Free public: hourly reanalysis via Open-Meteo's historical weather API (open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api, data CC BY 4.0) or the Copernicus Climate Data Store (free account; URL not confirmed this session). Yard addresses: a public trainer directory (source not confirmed).
card_time: Weather to yesterday midnight at each yard; reanalysis lags a few days, so the latest days come from forecast-archive analysis hours. Fixed before 06:00.
mechanism: Frozen, snowbound or waterlogged gallops stop fast work; the trainer knows which horses missed it, the market learns from results a fortnight later. The shock is exogenous, dated and shared by neighbouring yards, so it should lead the 'yard out of form' the market eventually prices; nearer the off, stable money and paddock condition move the price toward it.
nearest_known: Travel block (yard location to course), hot-form and connection windows (results-based yard form), course-weather lead 10. Step: weather where the horse is trained, as a leading cause of yard form rather than a lagging count of it.
novelty_check: Adjacent map: latent yard state 'none found' in racing. Repo: no weather served (reports/model_review_1111.md:73); NOAA weather held only at greyhound tracks. No dedicated web search; I have not seen yard-base weather modelled - unverified.
first_test: Build I for 2018-2026 as a drop-in block on the 11-fold screen with the placebo arm: pass at -0.0007 on log-BSP error; also the offset outcome model beyond BSP and the closing model with morningwap. Falsifier: the effect must be larger for runners off 40+ days and in winter for frost terms; if flat across those, reject.

title: Low-sun obstacle omission forecast from solar geometry and cloud
one_line: Compute at 06:00 the chance that fences or hurdles will be omitted for low sun at each jumps race, and tilt toward poor jumpers and flat-speed horses when it is high.
definition: For each jumps race: solar elevation e and azimuth a at the scheduled off (ephemeris from date, time, latitude, longitude). From open map geometry, the approach bearing t_k of each obstacle on the course in use. Glare index G = max over obstacles of 1[0 < e < e0] x max(0, cos(a - t_k)) x (1 - forecast low-cloud fraction at off time), e0 fitted (start 12 degrees - a guess). P(omission) = logistic in G by course, calibrated on recorded omissions. Runner features: G x jumping liability (fall, unseat and mistake rates; the jumps_form block's market view by obstacle), G x flat-speed rating, G x first time over the obstacle; all race-relative. Edge: races moved earlier in the day for light; hurdles and fences separately; zero for Flat.
data_needed: Free: solar ephemeris (computed), open map course and obstacle geometry (ODbL), cloud forecast and history (Open-Meteo, as above). Held: race_results (jumps runs, comments), jumps_form block inputs, betfair_prices morningwap 2018+. Omission history: no data found in the repository; result notes from a public results service would have to be collected.
card_time: Ephemeris and geometry are exact days ahead; cloud forecast from the 00 UTC run. Before 06:00.
mechanism: Omissions are decided by officials on the day, often minutes before the race, and remove several obstacles. Fewer jumps favours weak jumpers and speed over stamina-and-jumping types. The morning price is formed for the full course; the re-pricing comes at the announcement, which the sun's position and the cloud forecast largely determine hours earlier.
nearest_known: jumps_form block (fall rates, market view by obstacle); practitioners note omissions after the fact. Step: a card-time physical forecast of the omission and its interaction with jumping ability.
novelty_check: One web search (fences omitted, low sun, solar angle, model, betting): nothing on solar angle as a racing variable. Repo grep for 'low sun' and 'omitted': no hits.
first_test: Without omission history: jumps races Nov-Feb 2018-2026, G from ephemeris, geometry and reanalysis cloud; regress ln(morningwap/BSP) and the result-vs-BSP residual on G x jumping liability, walk-forward by season. Pass: t > 3 on the price move and sign right at two-thirds of courses with a west-facing run-in. Then collect omissions for 2 seasons to calibrate P(omission).

title: The void put: backs whose bad news ends in a withdrawal
one_line: A morning back is void if the horse comes out, so value each back by how often its trainer withdraws rather than runs when conditions turn against the horse.
definition: For runner i: A_i = chance of an adverse state today (going forecast to move at least one step against the horse's better side, plus a generic term). W_i = the trainer's shrunk rate of withdrawing declared runners in adverse states (k fitted; prior the trainer's overall rate, then the code's). d_i = mean log drift, morning to BSP, of comparable runners that did run in the adverse state for low-W trainers (the drift a void spares). Truncation value T_i = A_i x W_i x d_i. Use: expected CLV_i + T_i against the bar; stake tilt to high W when A is high. Also feed W_i x A_i to the closing model: a runner that a withdraw-prone trainer still runs is a positive signal. Edge: a void frees stake late in the window; charge the day's marginal CLV as opportunity cost.
data_needed: Held: 06:00 cards from 14 Jul 2026 against results (351 of 5,932 card runners did not run, 24 Oct-8 Nov, L:morning-card-gap-1110); live marks removals from 30 Sep 2026; going changes (L:card-vs-results-1110). Longer history: Betfair Historic BASIC market definitions Jan 2024+ if raw files are kept (not confirmed); trainer joined from the horse's nearest run, since race_results holds runners only.
card_time: W_i from history to yesterday; A_i from the card going and the weather forecast. Before 06:00.
mechanism: Bad news that ends in a withdrawal costs the backer nothing; the same news on a horse that runs is a drift laid at a loss at SP. Trainers differ in which they choose. The morning price averages over both states, but the backer's payoff is truncated in one of them - an option the price does not charge for.

Step: the bettor's own void as a truncation of the move distribution, added to expected CLV, and running-despite-adversity as a signal.

title: Intraday franking trade on scheduled form-line news
one_line: When a horse that recently met a later runner wins or flops earlier the same day, trade the later runner if its price has not yet moved by the amount form-line history implies.
definition: At 06:00 list, for every runner A, today's earlier runners B (off at least 20 minutes before A's) that met A in either's last 3 runs; weight w_AB = exp(-lengths between them / 3) x 0.85^(runs ago). Each B's race is a scheduled event. After B's result, surprise s_B = B's NFP minus the NFP expected from its BSP rank. Predicted move of A: d ln p_A = -theta x sum_B w_AB s_B, theta fitted on day-level history (rivals' later runs against the horse's next-run price). Trade: 2-5 minutes after B's result, if A's price has moved less than half the prediction and the remainder exceeds the spread plus 3%, back or lay A to the rule's stake; close at SP. Skip if A's off is within 15 minutes. Before the event, hold no resting order in A.
data_needed: Held: race_results for the links; betfair_live_marks from 30 Sep 2026 (60 s polls in the last hour, 300 s before); stream from 12 Nov 2026 for exact timing.
card_time: Links, weights and event times at 06:00; the trade itself is later in the day, after each earlier race.
mechanism: Franking is priced day to day here (rivals' later form moved prices: fu_ block -0.0046 on price, L:iter62). Within the day, few people watch a later race's exchange while an earlier race settles. The link list is knowable at 06:00 and the news arrives at a scheduled minute, so the only question is reaction speed, which recorded books can answer.
nearest_known: form_lines and form_uplift blocks (daily), franked-form lead 3 (reports/model_review_1111.md:85), in-day connection and draw features (rejected on outcome, L:confirm-holdout). Step: runner-to-runner links, within the day, traded on under-reaction rather than used as a 06:00 feature.

Pass: the BSP-minus-(+5 min) coefficient positive, day-clustered 90% interval above zero, paper CLV after 2% above zero. If the +5 minute price already holds the full move, close the idea.

title: Promotion-driven uninformed lay flow from extra-place offers
one_line: Bookmaker extra-place and each-way offers trigger matched bettors to lay the same runners on the exchange; forecast that price-insensitive flow per runner from the published terms and the arb gap.
definition: Per race: E = number of large bookmakers paying an extra place (and any enhanced place fraction), read from their published terms the evening before and at 06:00. Per runner: arb gap a_i = ln(best bookmaker price / exchange lay price); sweet spot q_i = 1 if the bookmaker price is between 6 and 21 (a guess, to be fitted); match rank r_i = within-race rank of a_i (how an odds-matching tool would list it). Predicted flow F_i = E x q_i x (1 - r_i/N). Features for the closing model: F_i for the win market and the same for place. Hypothesis to test, not assume: exchange price drifts out for high F_i between morning and off as lays arrive. Edge: zero when E = 0; cap E at the number of books recorded.

mechanism: Matched bettors back each-way at the bookmaker and lay win and place on the exchange, choosing runners by the closeness of the two prices, not by opinion. title: Quote-origin classification of the morning offer being taken
one_line: Classify each resting morning offer as an automated seed, a hedge or a directional order from its size and placement signature, and take seeds at a lower bar than directional offers.
definition: For each of the best 3 back offers on a runner at entry: size against the market's modal offer size across runners; whether the back and lay ladders sit symmetric around Betfair's catalogue forecast price or the bookmaker mid; ticks between the quote and that reference; whether the same size appears on many runners at once (one seeding program); quote age and refresh count (stream); a lone large lay-side offer on one runner only. Label by unsupervised mixture into seed / hedge / directional, then score each class by the realised CLV of taking it (walk-forward). Rule: bar of 1% on seed quotes, 3% on hedge, 8% on directional (guesses, to be fitted); the class also enters the closing model as a feature of the price being read.

Taking a stale seed is the edge already seen in the first hour (+10.5% at 06, L:live-by-hour-1104); taking a directional offer is adverse selection.

title: Trainer race-choice inverse model from entries and declarations
one_line: Model which of its entries a trainer chooses to declare, and read the departure from the public-information choice as the trainer's private view of the horse.
definition: Collect every horse's entries by stage, with which were declared. For each horse-week choice set C (races entered plus 'no run'), fit a conditional logit of the trainer's choice: utility = a x (public chance: market-rating share against the entered field) + b x ln prize + c x travel km + d x trip and going fit + e x days since run, with trainer random coefficients. For today's runner: r_i = utility of the chosen race minus the best forgone alternative under public information (negative = the trainer passed up an easier or richer race). Features: r_i; alternatives forgone; forward entries held within 14 days; declared here and elsewhere tomorrow; trainer-specific historical payoff of r (shrunk mean of next price move and A-E by r tercile). Edge: single-entry horses get r = 0 and a flag.
data_needed: Not held: entries history (reports/external_data_review.md:89 says dated copies may sit in the external scraper's storage - not opened). Fetchable now: 48-hour declarations (daily_predictions.py:579), forward only. Free public: the racing authorities' entries pages, forward capture; licence unchecked.
card_time: Entries and declarations are final 24-48 hours before; all known before 06:00.
mechanism: Choosing a harder race than the public rating warrants, or declining an obvious easy one, is a costly action by the person who knows the horse's work. Entries cost money and declarations commit the horse. The market sees today's card, not the menu the trainer chose from, so the choice is informative and largely unread.
nearest_known: Intent block (8 angle flags against the price), class-movement features, the unstored 'dated entries' noted in external_data_review. Step: a structural choice model over the trainer's own menu, with the residual as the feature.
novelty_check: One web search (trainer race selection, multiple entries, declarations, discrete choice, revealed preference): no paper models trainers' entry or declaration decisions; nearest is work on trainers' private information and betting (ueaeprints.uea.ac.uk/id/eprint/45782).
first_test: Fetchable first: the double-declaration flag from 48-hour declarations against withdrawal and ln(06:00 price/BSP) over 30+ days; pass t > 3 day-clustered. Then, with 6+ months of captured entries, r_i as a drop-in block on the screen (-0.0007 bar) and in the closing model.

title: Late-crowd salience from public attention data
one_line: Measure how visible each runner's jockey, trainer, owner and race are to casual bettors, and forecast the shortening that late recreational money gives salient runners after the morning.
definition: Per runner, salience S_i = mean of z-scores (against the same weekday over the past year) of daily page views, 7 days to D-1, for the encyclopedia articles of its jockey, trainer and (if any) the horse; plus owner is a racing club or large syndicate (owner string on the card, a field currently cut at daily_predictions.py:580); plus race shown on free-to-air television (published schedule). Race recreational share R = 1 - morning_vol / pp_vol from betfair_prices history, predicted at 06:00 by weekday, television, class, prize and course. Features: S_i minus field mean; (S_i minus field mean) x predicted R. Target: ln(morning price / BSP). Edge: no article = 0 with a missing flag; exclude the day itself to avoid reading the result.

Free public: Wikimedia page-view REST API, daily per article from July 2015 (URL and licence not confirmed this session); broadcaster schedules (history would need an archive - no source confirmed).

mechanism: The morning book is traded by a few informed accounts; casual money arrives in the last minutes and on televised days, and it follows names it recognises. That flow shortens salient runners between the morning and the SP whether or not they are better, which is exactly the move the live rule is paid on.

title: Hoof-traffic wear state since the last rail movement
one_line: Keep a running physical state of how worn each strip of each course is since the rail last moved, to forecast when the standing draw and pace bias will flip.
definition: Per course and track (round, straight): lanes of 2 m from the inner rail. After each race, add to lane l: runners x share of the field assumed in l (inner lanes fill first; share by field size and trip) x softness weight (going scale, soft cuts up more) x passes of that section. Between race days, decay U_l by exp(-days / tau), tau by growth conditions (soil temperature and rain; start 21 days - a guess). When rail_move changes by y yards, lanes inside y are set to protected and others shift. Features per race: U on the inner 3 lanes; fresh-strip flag and its width; racing days at the course in the last 7; each x stall (distance from rail), x projected early position, x going. Race-relative versions for the runner's likely lane.
data_needed: Held: race_results rail_move, runners, going, dates, stall, comments (2010+); draw engine's stall renumbering. Free: reanalysis weather for the recovery term (as above).
card_time: State to yesterday's last race; today's rail position from the card's rail_move where given (card coverage of that field not checked). Before 06:00.
mechanism: Draw and pace bias at a course is not fixed: it follows the ground's wear, which builds over a meeting and resets when the rail moves. Jockeys find it after the first races and prices follow. A state built from past traffic and the rail notice says before the first race which strip is fresh.
nearest_known: Draw engine (rail move flag, bias by course x trip x going with 730-day decay), GP draw surface, in-day draw slope (rejected, L:confirm-holdout). Step: a physical wear state per lane carried through time, instead of a fixed or slowly decayed course bias.
novelty_check: Maps: practitioners make daily track-bias notes by eye (world_practice section 7, 'unverified'); no cumulative wear model listed. No web search spent - unverified.

title: Decision-focused boosting through a smoothed entry rule
one_line: Train a forecast member whose loss is the trading rule's own profit, with gradients passed through a smoothed version of the entry decision, instead of price error.
definition: Custom LightGBM objective. Per runner: morning price m_i (morningwap), close b_i, output f_i = forecast ln BSP. Smoothed position q_i = sigmoid((ln m_i - f_i - bar) / T) x w_i, w_i = to-win stake weight 1/(m_i - 1) capped as the rule. Loss = -sum q_i x (m_i/b_i - 1 - cost) + lambda x (f_i - ln b_i)^2. Gradient in f_i = [q_i (1 - q_i/w_i) / T] x (m_i/b_i - 1 - cost) + 2 lambda (f_i - ln b_i); Hessian floored at a positive constant. Warm start from the served main member (init_score); anneal T from 0.10 to 0.02; bar 0.03; lambda chosen so the price error stays within the noise bar of the served member. Use as a fourth, gated member for entry decisions only, never for the published price.
data_needed: Held: betfair_prices morningwap and bsp 2018+ (no timestamps: morningwap is a proxy for the 06:00 price); the cached feature matrix; live marks from 30 Sep 2026 for the forward read.
card_time: A model member; scores at 06:00 like the others.
mechanism: The served members minimise price error over all runners, but the money is made only on the few where forecast and morning price disagree. A loss that weights exactly those runners, in the direction that pays, spends model capacity where the rule trades. The profit-weighted loss tried here re-weighted rows but never let the decision itself shape the gradient.
nearest_known: Profit-weighted asymmetric loss (+0.0147, reports/h2h_summary.md), race_xent member gated by the trade rule (L:iter105), steamer model on ln(morning/BSP). Step: the gradient flows through the entry decision (predict-then-optimise), with a price-error anchor.
novelty_check: From memory only: decision-focused learning is established in operations research and decorrelation losses exist in sports betting; I know of no racing use - unverified, no web search spent. Repo maps show no such objective.
first_test: Fit on the fast loop's cached matrix; score by the registered replay metric (CLV x stake after cuts on the rule) on walk-forward folds against the served blend. Pass: paired day bootstrap 90% interval above zero and price error not worse than +0.0007; count it in the ledger's trial tally.

title: Yard-base respiratory load from pollen and particulates
one_line: Cumulative pollen and fine-particle exposure at each training yard over the three weeks before a race, as a between-yard handicap on airway health the market cannot see.
definition: At each yard's coordinates, from the European air-quality reanalysis: daily grass and birch pollen, PM2.5, PM10 and ozone. Load L_p = exponentially weighted mean (half-life 7 days) over the 21 days to yesterday for pollutant p, standardised against that yard's own norm for the calendar week. Features: L_p; L_p minus the field mean; L_p x trip; L_p x the horse's respiratory flags (tongue-tie worn, declared wind operation where held, 'bled' or 'breathing' in past comments); L_p x age. Control: the same fields at the course on race day. Shrink yard sensitivity by empirical Bayes; missing pollen outside the season = 0 with a flag.

Held: race_results trainer, headgear, comments; yard centroids (model/blocks/travel.py). Yard addresses as in the training-interruption idea.
card_time: Exposure to yesterday at each yard; before 06:00.
mechanism: Airway inflammation is common in horses in training and is triggered by dust, pollen and pollutants. Race-day PM2.5 has been associated with slower winning speeds in 31,407 California races, 2011-2020 (per the cited summary). Three weeks of exposure where the horse lives should matter more than an afternoon at the track, and it differs between yards on the same card.

Also the 11-fold price screen. Expect a null as the base case; BSP has beaten 726 fundamental features (L:iter8-fundamental-no-blandford).

title: Forecast wind vector against run-in bearing for pace and rail bias
one_line: Resolve the forecast wind at off time into head and cross components along each course's straight, and interact them with projected early position and stall side.
definition: From open map geometry: bearing of the run-in and of the straight course at each track. From the weather forecast at the scheduled off: 10 m wind speed v, direction, gust. Headwind H = v x cos(wind-from bearing - running bearing); crosswind X = v x sin(same), signed toward the stands rail. Features: H x projected early-position score (lead probability from the pace engine); H x field size (cover available); H x trip; X x stall distance from the sheltered rail on straight courses; gust x first-time headgear. Race-relative. Thresholds: features zero below 4 m/s (a guess). Fit straight and round courses apart; history from reanalysis wind at the course.
data_needed: Held: race_results, pace engine outputs, stall, course coordinates. Free: open map geometry (ODbL), reanalysis and forecast wind via Open-Meteo (as above).
card_time: Wind forecast from the 00 UTC run for each off time; before 06:00.
mechanism: Into a headwind the leader pays the full drag and those behind shelter; a crosswind makes one rail the sheltered side. The bias shows in the first races and prices follow in the afternoon. The forecast vector is public at 06:00 but nobody resolves it along each course's straight and against the pace map.
nearest_known: Wind corrections inside speed figures (Ragozin, Thoro-Graph); folklore that a headwind favours closers; an informal tally on US ovals found no link (drf.com/news/answers-are-blowing-wind); one-off reports of wind-driven draw bias (racingpost.com, Ebor meeting). Step: a card-time forecast vector on straight courses, tested on the price move.
novelty_check: One web search (headwind, front runners, wind direction, draw bias, study): no rigorous study; forum and columnist material only. Repo grep for 'headwind' and 'wind_speed': no hits.
first_test: 2018-2026 with reanalysis wind: H x early position and X x stall on the result-vs-BSP residual and on ln(morningwap/BSP), walk-forward by year. Pass: t > 3 on the price move, same sign at two-thirds of straight courses. The pace and draw rebuilds found nothing unconditional (L:iter18, iter25), so a null here closes wind as their missing condition.

title: Trainer excuse validity from official post-race explanations
one_line: Code the regulator's published post-race explanations and vet findings into causes, and score each trainer on whether horses given that excuse later beat the market's expectation.
definition: From each meeting's published stewards' report: for every horse named, extract (by a language model with a fixed 20-class scheme) the cause (going, trip, breathing, bled, lame, lost shoe, in season, hung, no explanation), who stated it (vet-confirmed or trainer-stated), and the trigger (ran below or above market expectation). Features at the next run: cause class; cause removed today (going differs, trip changed, tongue-tie or wind operation since); V_tc = trainer t's shrunk mean, for cause c, of the next-run change in market rating and of won minus BSP probability (k fitted; prior the cause's mean); a 'no explanation offered' flag; count of prior explanations for the horse. As-of rule: only reports published before the race day.
data_needed: Free public: the regulators' stewards' reports pages for Britain and Ireland (URL, history depth and terms not confirmed this session). Held: race_results, market_rating block for the scoring. Not held: any stewards' or vet data for UK/IE (repo_data map).
card_time: Reports are published within a day of each meeting; all prior runs' reports known before 06:00.
mechanism: An official explanation is a statement by the trainer, on the record, about why the last run should be ignored, and a vet finding is hard evidence. The market reads the famous ones; it cannot easily know which trainers' stated excuses are followed by improvement and which are routine cover. That per-trainer validity is learnable only from the coded history.
nearest_known: Comment classes (retired, L:iter45), Hong Kong vet records and Australian stewards' reports in practice, wind-operation statistics. Step: the British and Irish official explanations coded by cause and source, with trainer-specific validity scored against the market rating.
novelty_check: Academic map: language-model work on stewards' reports is journalism and student work only. Repo: 'stewards' reports' appears only for Australia (reports/international_racing.md:29). No dedicated web search - unverified.
first_test: Collect two seasons; build the block; 11-fold screen with placebo (-0.0007) and the offset outcome model. Pass on either with intervals excluding zero. Falsifier: V_tc must predict out of sample for trainers with 30+ coded explanations; if it does not persist (as entity residuals did not, L:iter11-ae), retire.
